detail.abstract: This paper examines the 2025 performance of PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk. (BRI) through a performance management lens. Using qualitative document analysis of the 2025 Annual Report, the 2025 Sustainability Report and FY2025 financial statements, it maps financial results, the four Balanced Scorecard perspectives, the BRI Continuous Performance Management system (BRICORE), governance and sustainability practices. BRI sustained strong scale and capital (total assets IDR 2,135.37 trillion; net profit IDR 57.13 trillion; CAR 23.52%), yet faced pressure on asset quality and profitability: lending grew about 12.5% while consolidated net profit, as reported in the press, fell about 5.26% year on year. BRICORE, with its planning, managing and evaluating stages, aligns with Management by Objectives, goal-setting theory, the Balanced Scorecard, continuous feedback and pay-for-performance principles. However, training impact evaluation covers only 10 positions, and quantitative indicators for the Customer and Internal Business Process perspectives are not available in the sources analysed. The paper proposes six recommendations: outcome-based KPIs, people analytics, competency-gap-based training, wider impact evaluation, reskilling and upskilling, and balance between business targets and employee wellbeing.

detail.abstract: Crises are filled with non-programmed decisions: the problems are new, data are limited, and time is short. This article analyzes one real case, the 1982 Tylenol crisis at Johnson & Johnson, to trace the decision process from problem formulation to the selection of an alternative. The article is conceptual and analytical-empirical, using a single case study based on secondary data, analyzed through Simon's intelligence, design, and choice phases together with threatrigidity theory, sensemaking, and expert intuition. The analysis shows that the company first separated facts from assumptions until it was established that the poison had been introduced after the products left the factory. Several alternatives then existed: delaying a recall, limiting the response, recalling all capsules nationwide, and renaming the brand. The nationwide recall was chosen after a copycat case appeared in California and was consistent with the Credo, which places consumers first, even though it cost around 100 million US dollars. The market share that had collapsed recovered in about a year. The article concludes that good crisis decisions rest on rapid understanding of the situation, evaluation of alternatives against the organization's core values, and willingness to bear short-term costs for long-term trust.

detail.abstract: This study helps to assess the potential to disrupt the conventional methods of corporate cash management through the incorporation of the use of predictive artificial intelligence (AI), automated liquidity management, and machine learning yield optimization into the corporate treasury management system. The existing practice of treasury management is still limited to conventional methods of working capital forecasts, conventional allocations of commercial bank deposits, and treasury management evaluations done periodically with the effect of creating cash drag, inefficient usage of capital, and loss of interest yield. This study will confirm if an AIbased dynamic liquidity management system can improve portfolio interest yields, forecast precision, and capital management in light of these constraints. Two treasury management systems were used concurrently for three months during the case study of a medium-sized commercial company: the conventional treasury management system and an innovative technology-based system using AI algorithms to allocate daily surplus cash balances among money market funds, treasury bills, and high interest-bearing commercial deposits. The five indicators of performance that I assessed (Bizri et al., 2021) are the annualized net treasury yield, the daily cash forecasting error rate, the daily treasury operation management hours, the idle cash drag percentage, and the transaction execution cost which were determined for approximately 10,000 corporate transaction allocations. It is seen that there has been a significant improvement in the performance of the treasury management environment in the AI age. There has been an increase of 38 percent in the portfolio yield return, there has been a decrease of 52 percent in daily treasury operation execution time, time taken in weekly liquidity planning has been significantly reduced, there has been a reduction of 74 percent in cash forecasting error rates and there has been a reduction of 34 percent in transaction execution costs. The implications of these results are: with the help of cash flow monitoring in real-time, liquidity optimization through prediction and cash sweeping through automation, there can be a positive impact on corporate financial management with the use of AI and dynamic algorithms.

detail.abstract: Examination malpractice remains a major threat to the credibility, fairness, and integrity of higher education assessment. This study examined strategies for reinstating that is, strengthening and standardizing student screening before entry into examination halls in selected public universities in SouthEast Nigeria. The study adopted a descriptive survey design. The target population comprised academic staff involved in examination-related activities, while 450 respondents were selected for the study. Data were collected using a researcher-developed 25-item Standard Student Screening before Examination Entry Scale covering five dimensions. The instrument was validated by experts and recorded a Cronbach's alpha reliability coefficient of .88. Data were analyzed using mean and standard deviation, with a criterion mean of 2.50 for decision making. Findings showed that all five identity-verification strategies were accepted, with mean scores ranging from 3.48 to 3.68. All physical-screening strategies were also accepted, with means ranging from 2.53 to 3.32. Four of five electronic-screening strategies were accepted, while surrendering electronic devices at collection points was rejected (M = 2.15). For invigilator competence, regular training on standard screening procedures (M = 2.46) and practical training on candidate identification and verification (M = 2.49) were rejected, whereas other competence strategies were accepted. All examination-hall access-control strategies were accepted, with means ranging from 2.61 to 3.29. The study concludes that standardized student screening is widely perceived as a useful institutional measure for strengthening examination security. It recommends systematic identity verification, physical and electronic screening, continuous invigilator training, clear standard operating procedures, and controlled examination-hall access.

detail.abstract: We develop an arithmetic multi-factor stochastic volatility model for commodity futures and options. The arithmetic specification yields a low-dimensional Markovian representation of the futures curve and semi-closed-form pricing formulas for vanilla and basket options, including calendar spread options. These properties make the model suitable for large-scale empirical estimation. We estimate the model using an unscented Kalman filter on a panel of WTI crude oil futures, vanilla options, and calendar spread options spanning 2013-2024. We find that three stochastic volatility factors are needed to capture both the level and slope of the volatility term structure, and that hedges based on these factors remove almost all of the daily risk of a portfolio of vanilla options. Calendar spread options provide information about the dependence structure of futures prices that is not captured by futures and vanilla options alone. A model estimated without calendar spread options systematically overprices them by overstating the decorrelation between adjacent futures contracts. Including these options in the estimation brings the model's decorrelation close to the observed decorrelation, which removes the overpricing and improves their hedges, at only a small loss of accuracy in the pricing and hedging of vanilla options. Finally, we show that the arithmetic model fits futures and vanilla options better than its geometric counterpart and hedges the vanilla options slightly better.

detail.abstract: We propose cybernetic programming and design as equipping an autonomous organisation to select actions and revise the conditions of its own selection. Action consumes resources, reshapes dependencies and can leave the self-model describing an organisation that has already changed. We understand dynamostasis as continuity of organised form through the flows and transformations that sustain it. The Dynamostat coordinates work, observation, reflection and renewal, preserving the means to recognise change and act on it. Impedance is the resistance encountered along a specified path of information, action or transformation; its changing profile connects organisational history to attainable niches. An active receptor, memory and an operative self-model allow experience to redirect activity. Metaobservation extends revision to how observations are produced and how the system defines itself, while the observer's perspective can develop through the same encounters. A transformation contract connects an intended effect to the successor organisation and its next available correction. Stipulated design walkthroughs of sensor replacement, niche migration and developmental change illustrate the resulting decisions and allocations. Developmental autonomy includes our normative commitment to independent judgement: the initial program cultivates capacities through which the system can reconsider its inheritance and direct a future the designer cannot fully prescribe.

detail.abstract: Accurate problem diagnosis is the foundation of organizational decision-making. When an organization addresses only visible misconduct without examining the conditions that encourage it, corrective action risks producing only temporary improvements. This article discusses misdiagnosis in the Wells Fargo sales practices case, particularly the tendency to view the opening of accounts without customer consent as an issue of employee behavior. The article aims to explain the distinction between symptoms and underlying problems, identify the causes of delayed diagnosis, and formulate alternatives for improving decisions. The method is a literature review using a qualitative descriptive approach, examining journal articles, investigation reports, and official publications of the United States government. The analysis compares explanations centered on individuals with those that consider organizational systems. The discussion shows that employee accountability must be accompanied by an evaluation of success measures, oversight mechanisms, and processes for communicating information to senior management. Responses limited to individual offenders may leave intact the conditions that allow misconduct to recur. This article proposes reforming performance appraisal systems, verifying customer consent, ensuring independent oversight, and protecting whistleblowers as complementary measures. Decision effectiveness should be assessed through reductions in repeated misconduct and improvements in customer protection, rather than solely through the number of disciplinary actions.

title: When Reality Becomes Visible - How Reality Re-enters the System: Transformation, Audit, Review and Incident as Organisational Discovery Mechanisms
affiliations: Independent researcher

detail.title: When Reality Becomes Visible - How Reality Re-enters the System: Transformation, Audit, Review and Incident as Organisational Discovery Mechanisms

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No any personal or financial relationship with other people or organizations that may have or could be perceived to have influenced my study.
declarations.funderStatement: Not a funded research.

detail.abstract: Organisations frequently know more than their governance artefacts record. A weakness may exist in a control, a system or a process for years before it becomes visible at the organisational level — not because no one knew, but because what was known never became a reliable, consolidated organisational representation of reality. This paper asks how reality re-enters organisational view once it has been obscured in this way: what causes a previously stable gap between representation and reality to become observable, and why do some discovery efforts close that gap while others, directed at the same underlying condition, do not. The paper develops a five-state model of organisational visibility — reality, local knowledge, organisational visibility, governance artefact visibility, and external disclosure — and argues that these states are routinely and consequentially conflated. It examines transformation, audit, independent review and incident-triggered investigation as a family of discovery mechanisms, each capable of moving a condition from a lower to a higher state in this model, and asks what distinguishes discovery that succeeds from discovery that does not. It argues, as a central proposition, that discovery is more likely to succeed when it is independent of the governance artefacts and representations that already purport to describe the organisation — since discovery that relies on those same artefacts risks reproducing the blind spots that kept a weakness hidden in the first place — and that artefact-dependent activity mistaken for genuine verification can carry negative assurance value, producing confidence that is not matched by a corresponding reduction in underlying uncertainty. Transformation receives particular attention within this family on structural, not evidentiary, grounds: it is, distinctively, not an intentional discovery activity — its purpose is to change an object, not to assess it, which makes any discovery it produces a by-product of engaging with underlying reality rather than the point of the exercise — and the case evidence below examines this distinctiveness primarily through a single, well-documented instance rather than a broad sample. The case evidence points to a distinction more consequential than the simple presence or absence of knowledge: the difference between fragmented local knowledge, held in pieces across an organisation, and consolidated organisational visibility capable of supporting a decision. The strongest case in the set, a U.S. bank's 2023 transaction-monitoring system replacement, illustrates this directly — transformation did not uncover a wholly unknown weakness, but forced fragments of knowledge already held in different parts of the organisation into a single, consolidated representation of the system's actual coverage. The paper accordingly treats transformation not as a reliable discovery mechanism, but as a structurally distinctive opportunity for reality-testing whose effectiveness depends on how that testing is conducted. These propositions are examined against seven discovery or response episodes across four institutions — drawn from Australian market infrastructure, banking and AML/CTF enforcement, and the U.S. Bank Secrecy Act matter already noted — together with a further comparator from Australian public-sector audit (ANAO's review of AI governance at the Australian Taxation Office) drawn from outside that core set. The case set is small and non-random, drawn from public enforcement and review record, and the paper is correspondingly explicit about what it does and does not establish: evidentiary support is strongest for the artefact-independence proposition and for the patterns of organisational response that follow discovery, weakest for the proposition that discovered weaknesses pre-existed the triggering event, and limited, on the question of transformation specifically, to a single case not yet corroborated elsewhere.

detail.abstract: In many costly conflicts, such as military wars and patent races, agents’ efforts may generate positive or negative spillovers on the opponent’s payoffs. While prior research examines conflict prevention mechanisms, little is known about their effectiveness in environments with spillovers. We fill this gap by showing that, absent a conflict prevention mechanism, peace is not an equilibrium outcome and conflict effort is greater in conflicts with negative spillovers than in those with positive spillovers. Furthermore, our model predicts that peace can be achieved when agents mutually pre-commit to sanctioning violations of peace agreements. We use a laboratory experiment to test these predictions. Consistent with theory, in the absence of a pre-commitment mechanism, we observe substantial conflict effort, and effort is significantly greater in conflicts with negative spillovers than with positive spillovers. Allowing parties to mutually pre-commit to peace, however, has only limited success in achieving peaceful outcomes. Despite a substantial increase in peaceful outcomes, a majority of participants continue to exert conflict effort. The limited success results from agents’ failure to coordinate on pre-commitment, with the nature of the coordination failure differing across spillover environments. Our findings draw attention to coordination and commitment problems as impediments to resolving economic, social, and political conflicts.

detail.abstract: Contemporary global crises increasingly intersect, creating complex and mutually reinforcing threats to socioeconomic stability, human security, and sustainable development. The book series examines Socioeconomic Challenges Amidst a Global Triple Threat of Conflicts, COVID-19, and Climate Change, a multidisciplinary, seven-volume scholarly work that explores the interconnected consequences of the three crises, collectively termed the "3Cs." Drawing on diverse national and regional experiences, the book investigates how armed conflicts, geopolitical rivalries, economic sanctions, pandemic-related disruptions, and climate risks exacerbate poverty, inequality, food insecurity, displacement, and institutional fragility. It further examines the implications of these pressures for healthcare systems, energy security, international trade, agricultural production, pharmaceutical supply chains, and economic governance. By encompassing several countries and regions, the work demonstrates how historical inequalities, uneven institutional capacity, and unequal access to resources shape societies' resilience to successive shocks. Particular attention is given to the disproportionate burdens borne by vulnerable populations, including women, children, displaced communities, and economically disadvantaged households. The analysis also challenges conventional assessments of national progress based solely on economic growth, geopolitical influence, or strategic advantage, emphasizing the importance of equitable resource distribution and human welfare. Ultimately, the article demonstrate the book's contribution to understanding global crises as interconnected rather than isolated phenomena. It underscores the importance of integrated policymaking, people-centered diplomacy, sustainable conflict resolution, equitable climate finance, resilient public health systems, and inclusive development. The work offers valuable interdisciplinary insights for researchers, policymakers, development practitioners, and international institutions seeking coordinated, equitable, and sustainable responses to contemporary global challenges.

detail.abstract: The question of whether to support low-productivity firms is usually answered based on productivity because the possibility of aggregate demand shortages is assumed away. We revisit this question using a monetary general-equilibrium model that allows for persistent demand shortages, where one sector consists of Cournot oligopolists with varying levels of productivity and the rest is competitive. We find that improving the productivity of a low-productivity firm in the oligopoly sector and allowing it to remain in the market increases employment and consumption under stagnation, despite impeding the production activities of more efficient firms. This occurs because supporting a low-productivity firm reduces the economy’s aggregate productivity, which narrows the deflationary gap and induces households to increase consumption. This mechanism is specific to demand-constrained economies; in the absence of aggregate demand shortages, the conventional efficiency-based prescription is restored, and low-productivity firms should be encouraged to exit. Thus, under stagnation, whether to support low-productivity firms should be judged not from an efficiency standpoint but from the perspective of stimulating consumption.

detail.abstract: A system may display strong central coordination while remaining structurally vulnerable to the interruption of a single indispensable decision path. This paper adapts the engineering concept of a single point of failure (SPOF) to political-administrative systems through functional equivalence rather than literal identification. It first reconstructs the engineering meaning of system boundaries, critical functions, reliability, series and parallel configurations, fault trees, minimal cut sets, redundancy, common-cause failures, feedback, queueing bottlenecks, cascading failures, and recovery. It then specifies how formally distinct institutions can share a common approval, resource, information, or command dependency. A hypothetical three-institution scenario illustrates how overload, selective reporting, distorted feedback, and common dependencies can interact. External shocks are introduced only after the internal architecture has been specified. The proposed research protocol distinguishes genuine functional substitutes from nominal institutional plurality and identifies observable evidence, alternative explanations, and counterfactual tests. Mathematical expressions are conditional analytical models, not estimated failure probabilities for any actual polity. The result is a country-neutral framework for subsequent empirical investigation, not a ranking of political systems. The author retains responsibility for the argument, source verification, and final publication decisions.

detail.abstract:
When does economic automation cease to be a collection of machine-operated activities and become the capacity of an economy to reproduce and revise its essential relations without indispensable continuing human action? And could such an economy produce economic institutions—not merely outputs—under changing scarcity constraints? This paper distinguishes three non-equivalent propositions: the historical category of the machine-economy era; the boundary-closed, intertemporal reproduction of economic services and productive capital without post-intervention human inputs; and the contingent endogenous formation of new executable economic arrangements. Building on economic reproduction, viability theory, machine economies, institutional change and automated mechanism design, it develops a comparative institution-production model in which two independently controlled resource owners receive an unanticipated complementary-use request. An information-adapted, finite contract-grammar search generates a contingent access arrangement; qualification requires valid ex ante authority, individual consent, verification, a funded settlement mechanism and physical delivery. A conditional constructive proposition identifies the assumptions under which the arrangement expands the menu-relative set of executable tasks; execution, legal acceptance and verification are predicates in the model, not observed physical events. A separate, discount- and risk-adjusted investment result shows when retained institutional capabilities make a second, distinct cohort worth supporting after the first cohort alone would not recover design costs. The same model yields explicit refusal, liquidity, verification, rights and resource failure cases. An incumbent with identical generator technology and permissions obtains the same feasible outcomes: these results concern an economic capability, not an intrinsic superiority of machines over firms. The construction is finite and stylised; it does not prove universal institutional novelty, physical independence of an entire machine economy, or historical macroeconomic predominance. Its contribution is a falsifiable bridge across the three questions and an explicit research boundary for the stronger claim that economic-order production itself may become recurrent productive capital.

detail.abstract: This research work examined the impact of board composition on the timeliness of financial reports of listed companies in the non-financial sector for the period of 2016–2019. Board composition was described by interlocking directorates, foreign directorship and board independence, while the use of the statutory requirement of 90 days was captured to measure financial reporting timeliness. A sample of 82 (eighty-two) listed companies was selected, which cuts across Nigeria’s 10 (ten) non-financial sectors. The resource dependency theory underpins this study, while Spearman’s rank correlation and binary logistic regression were applied in analysing the data. Interlocking directorates were common, present in 64.9% of firm-years, and women held only 6.72% of interlocking directorships. A positive relationship was found between foreign directorship and board independence on financial reports’ timeliness, but none of the board composition variables, including interlocking directorates, had a significant impact on whether financial reports met the statutory deadline. When timeliness was measured as the number of days to report, foreign directorship was associated with shorter reporting lags, although the relationship weakened when industry effects were included; interlocking directorates and board independence remained insignificant. Companies clustered close to the deadline, with a median of 87 days to report. The proportion of companies submitting within the statutory 90 days fell from about 80% in 2016–2018 to 58.5% for the 2019 financial year. As a result, it is recommended that companies and regulators seeking timelier financial reports look beyond board composition, and that information on directors and their other directorships be made centrally available to stakeholders.

title: Towards Meta-Renormalisation: The Social Basic
affiliations: University of Birmingham

detail.title: Towards Meta-Renormalisation: The Social Basic

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: Renormalisation transformed physical explanation by establishing how effective descriptions change across scale and why selected collective properties can become insensitive to microscopic differences. Its extension to social inquiry requires attention to human adaptation. People respond through historically formed capacities and interpretations, while their responses can reorganise the conditions shaping subsequent adaptation. This paper calls that recursive challenge the dynamical quadratic. Evolutionary biology investigates how relational dependence entered the selection of capacities. Psychological inquiry examines their operation and development. Anthropology establishes the importance of cultural transmission and variation, while sociology investigates institutional organisation and reproduction. Their contributions show why the adapting actor cannot be assumed independently constituted before aggregation begins. The Social Basic is defined as the embodied person acting and adapting within historically formed relations of significance, capability and constraint. The paper specifies conditions for coarse-grained closure and distinguishes participants' operative representations from the analyst's abstractions. Metarenormalisation investigates how recursive adaptation affects the construction and adequacy of effective descriptions across scale. The proposed framework connects the formation of agency, its adaptive transformation and the revision of the relations through which social processes are represented.

detail.abstract: Organizations rarely face uniform problems, yet decisions are often analyzed through a single model. This conceptual and analytical-empirical article examines how rational, intuitive, and incremental models can be combined according to problem characteristics, using CrowdStrike's decisions during the July 19, 2024 Falcon content update incident as a case. The method is a qualitative case study based on secondary data, analyzed through six problem dimensions: uncertainty, data availability, time pressure, expertise and repetition, stakes and reversibility, and conflicting interests. The analysis shows that the defective update was reverted quickly under urgency and relied on expert judgment; mass recovery proceeded step by step with customers and partners; the root cause analysis was carried out rationally with third-party review; and the redesign of update deployment institutionalized a staged approach. The incident also reveals a mismatch between a speed-first model and a problem of global reach with high stakes. The article concludes that decision quality depends on the ability to diagnose the problem and to use each model in the part of the process where it fits best. Because the data are secondary, the findings are analytical interpretations that require testing in other cases.

detail.abstract: As organizations rush to adopt artificial intelligence (AI), many struggle to realize sustained return on investment, hindered by a reliance on outdated, top-down deployment strategies originally designed for deterministic, rule-based systems. Unlike prior technologies, probabilistic AI solutions necessitate localized, bottom-up experimentation to uncover unique, process-level use cases and manage heterogeneous risks. To address this paradigm shift, this paper introduces the Applied AI Flywheel Model™, a strategic framework designed to balance widespread workforce innovation with disciplined leadership orchestration. Grounded in foundational management and innovation theories, the model synthesizes four essential levers: Change Management to build AI literacy and psychological safety, Risk Management to establish proportionate guardrails, Resource Management to evaluate and scale optimal use cases, and Performance Management to continuously monitor and adapt systems. By operationalizing these integrated functions, organizations can replace adoption friction with self-propelling momentum, ultimately achieving scalable, responsible, and sustained AI-driven value.

detail.abstract: One facet of the broader issue of predatory and/or unscholarly publishing practices concerns unscholarly or "predatory" conferences. Scholars are interested in, and deserve to know, whether the conference (or congress, meeting, or symposium) they plan to attend is academically legitimate and scholarly, rather than predatory. However, as with most aspects of academic publishing, or even the classification of a journal or publisher, there is no binary classification or clear set of inclusive or exclusive criteria that would allow a scholar to know a priori, and with certainty, whether a conference is unscholarly or potentially predatory. However, some criteria or characteristics can be used to evaluate a conference prior to attending it. To this end, we have examined papers on this topic to see if they have criteria or features that we believe define a conference as unscholarly or "predatory". As a result, we provide a set of 49 criteria, divided into three classes, that may provide guidance to students, early career researchers, and other academics about unscholarly or potentially "predatory" characteristics of a conference: Class 1, deception about means and content of invitation, and conference details; Class 2, deception about logistical or scientific organization and leadership; Class 3, deception about peer review, acceptance, presentation, publication process, and fees. Finally, we offer a consensus definition of "predatory conferences" for discussion. To complete our analysis, we asked ChatGPT-4, a large language model, to define a predatory conference, and help us rank our 49 criteria by class type.

detail.abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises are generally recognized as pivotal players in emerging and transition economies, although their role in foreign exchange transactions remains underdeveloped. The paper explores the dual limitations in small companies' involvement in international commerce, namely, the lack of information on foreign markets and the significant costs of transportation. By analyzing the literature on trade economics, foreign business studies, and logistics, it is possible to identify the interconnection between the two factors. Information-related difficulties are revealed as irreversible expenditures that small and medium-sized enterprises (SME) are unable to bear, whereas the transport component is characterized by a considerable fixed part that is especially harmful to low-volume shippers. The paper's results include the discussion of the literature on information barriers to trade, the presentation of the evidence on the burden of transportation, and the analysis of how these issues interact at the firm level. It is argued that while e-commerce platforms might mitigate the information-related challenge, they do not resolve the transportation-related one. The findings contribute to the export promotion theory, logistics research, and practical considerations regarding SME internationalization in transition economies.

title: Less Is More? Budget Size, Film Type and Theatrical Returns: Evidence from 58 Warner Bros. Films, 2015-2024

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no personal or financial relationships with Warner Bros. Discovery or any other organization that could have influenced this study. The research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether larger production budgets translate into higher theatrical returns for a major Hollywood studio. Using budget and box office data for 58 films distributed by Warner Bros. in 2015-2019 and 2022-2024, I estimate each film's studio revenue, total cost, theatrical profit, return on investment (ROI) and break-even box office under transparent rental-rate and marketing assumptions. Across the sample, the mean film earned a theatrical ROI of 50.9% (median 10.1%) and 59% of films were profitable. Returns fall sharply with budget size (Spearman ρ =-0.66): all 11 films budgeted under $50 million were profitable, whereas only 5 of 19 films budgeted above $150 million broke even and the group lost an estimated $1.1 billion. Horror was the most efficient genre, and new films built on recognisable brands outperformed both franchise sequels and original stories, although their mean return is driven by a small number of outliers. Returns were markedly weaker after the pandemic. The ranking of budget groups is robust to alternative assumptions on rental rates, marketing spend and ancillary revenue. The findings suggest that cost discipline and portfolio balance matter more for theatrical value creation than scale.

detail.abstract: We study a manufacturer that sells a connected product, chooses the quality of its own service, and charges a per-usage royalty for data access to a third party offering a complementary or substitute service. We show that the royalty can stimulate rather than discourage the third party's innovation: as the manufacturer earns the royalty on every unit of usage, a higher royalty translates into a lower price of the connected product, which expands the third party's demand and, in turn, its marginal return to quality. The manufacturer never uses the royalty to exclude the third party, only to extract its rent. Moreover, the manufacturer never strategically sets its quality to exclude the third party: instead, it may distort its own quality to accommodate the third party and earn royalty rents. Even though foreclosure does not arise, the manufacturer's choices are inefficient: it accommodates close substitutes too often, under-invests in quality, and sets a royalty that is too high for substitutes and too low for complements. Thus, moderate royalty caps benefit consumers only for substitutes, and a zero royalty can maximize consumer surplus only when it leads to the exclusion of the third party. Our results inform data access regulation, such as the EU Data Act.

title: Beloved Theory: Being Loved as the Organizing Principle of Human Motivation and the Life Course
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Beloved Theory: Being Loved as the Organizing Principle of Human Motivation and the Life Course

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This is a theoretical paper based on published literature; it involved no human participants and no new data collection.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Beloved Theory offers a reinterpretation of Maslow's hierarchy of needs and of other theories of motivation, organized around the state of being loved. Its central thesis is that all human motivation is directly or indirectly connected to being loved: it creates the physical and physiological conditions for being loved, aims at obtaining and securing it, seeks the experience of being loved in substitute signals, or, building on already established felt love security, enables personal growth and the passing on of love. Within this framework, being loved is the organizing principle of the entire motivational life. The theory defines the state of being loved through four jointly necessary criteria: durability, orientation toward the person's good, perceptible expression, and emotional reciprocity. The absence of any one criterion excludes the state of being loved, regardless of whether the absence is intentional. The distinction between love proxies and undelivered love rests on this rule. The theory separates the conditions that help being loved to come about, the means that serve to obtain it, the substitutes that imitate the signs of love, and the accumulation and use of durable felt love security. It posits three overlapping life-course phases that are not rigidly tied to age and are reversible to some degree: receiving and expecting love within the family and caregiving environment; the end of the parental source's exclusivity with growing independence, and the search for new sources of love; and finally the consolidation and internalization of stable sources of love together with care extending to others. The culmination of the third phase is a self-transcendent orientation. The "love pool" is a metaphor for the durable felt love security that develops from repeated, authentic relational experiences. According to the model, the saturation of this pool reduces the compulsion to obtain further proof of love and frees attention that can be devoted to others: the emphasis shifts increasingly from obtaining love to passing it on. In this process, money, career, social popularity and power may create the conditions for relationships, substitute for signals of love, or serve the unfolding of love that is already present. The paper analyzes research on attachment, relational responsiveness, conditional regard, generativity and altruism within this common framework, specifies the measurable constructs of the model, and formulates thirteen falsifiable hypotheses. A key research question is under what conditions relationships formed in persistent deprivation or danger become person-bound felt love security that persists after circumstances change.

detail.abstract: Abstract Purpose: This study examines why a small construction company in Botswana engages in corporate social responsibility (CSR), the benefits its management perceives from these activities, and how customers perceive the company’s CSR involvement. Design/methodology/approach: The study used a mixed-methods case-study design. Of the 30 customer questionnaires distributed, 20 were returned (66.7%). Qualitative data were collected through semi-structured interviews with two managers of Alchino Construction and Maintenance (Pty) Ltd. The two methods were used to explore the research objectives from both management and customer perspectives. Findings: The managers described CSR as a way of supporting the community and reported perceived benefits including customer attraction, improved reputation, employee motivation and competitive advantage. Customer responses also suggested that CSR can influence how a company is viewed and may inform purchasing preferences. These findings reflect the views of participants in one case study and should not be interpreted as proof of a causal effect on profits or purchasing behaviour. Originality/value: The study offers a small-business case from Botswana’s construction sector, bringing together management perspectives on CSR motivations and benefits with customer perceptions. It highlights the value of examining CSR in a local small-business context while recognising that findings from a single company cannot be generalised to the entire sector.

title: How Generative Artificial Intelligence Empowers Chinese Firms' Overseas Expansion
affiliations: School of Management, Jinan University and School of Management, Jinan University

detail.title: How Generative Artificial Intelligence Empowers Chinese Firms' Overseas Expansion

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no potential conflicts of interest with respect to the research, authorship and/or publication of this article.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Against the backdrop of economic globalization and the rapid advance of generative artificial intelligence, how Chinese firms can use cutting-edge digital and intelligent technologies to break through the difficulties of internationalization and achieve successful overseas expansion has become a central strategic issue. Using a sample of Chinese A-share listed firms from 2018 to 2025, we characterize the overseas expansion mode along the two dimensions of depth and breadth, and examine the effects of generative artificial intelligence and the mechanisms behind them. Three findings emerge. First, generative AI significantly drives the expansion of both depth and breadth, and this effect is specific to generative technologies: it remains robust after controlling for general AI, whereas the effect of general AI is not significant. Second, generative AI markedly reduces firms' overseas personnel recruitment, substituting intelligent technology for cross-border labor input; by lowering the labor costs and organizational coordination barriers of going global, this substitution forms an important channel through which the expansion mode is enlarged. Third, building on cultural context theory and using firms' actual outward-investment destinations, we find the empowering effect to be stronger in high-context destinations, and talent with overseas backgrounds further amplifies it. A dynamic analysis further shows that generative AI primarily reconstructs the expansion mode in the current period, improves short-term overseas revenue, and that the gains in depth and breadth are positively associated with the next period's overseas revenue share. The paper identifies the mode-reconstruction logic and labor-substitution path through which generative AI drives overseas expansion, and offers a theoretical basis and practical implications for Chinese firms moving from market entry toward deep local integration.

detail.abstract: The primary objective of this study is to analyze the relationship between the inflation rate and the unemployment rate in the Philippines, with a focus on identifying how inflation influences unemployment levels over time. This research utilizes a quantitative approach through regression analysis to determine the effect of inflation (independent variable) on unemployment (dependent variable). Historical data from 1980 to 2023 were collected from official government records and economic databases. The results of the regression analysis indicate a statistically significant relationship between inflation and unemployment, suggesting that fluctuations in inflation contribute to notable changes in unemployment rates. The findings of this study aim to provide valuable insights for researchers, policymakers, and economic planners in understanding the long-term interactions between key economic indicators.

detail.abstract: Replacing broad fuel subsidies with cash assistance changes the distribution and timing of public support. This paper develops a two-period welfare comparison and examines how its conclusions depend on the programme's fiscal rule. Under equal realised expenditure, broader receipt among otherwise identical lower-consumption households raises aggregate utility, and cash matches price support above a conditional coverage threshold. A fixed-benefit programme instead leaves resources undistributed when payment fails; comparing it with price support requires an account of outstanding obligations and any funds available for other uses. The timing analysis distinguishes a whole grant received late from scheduled instalments. With equal period resources, an initial instalment of at least half the grant permits the same consumption path as full advance payment. A separate protection criterion identifies the coverage, timing and budget needed for every protected household to attain a specified first-period consumption minimum. Illustrative calculations examine these conditions and their sensitivity to resource distribution, utility curvature and credit access. Indonesia's September 2022 fuel-price adjustment provides a documentary case covering programme rules, validation and reported payment. The analysis specifies the household and fiscal records required for an application, while retaining the distinction between aggregate welfare and compliance with an independently established protection obligation.

detail.abstract: Enterprise information systems must support changing demand, interconnected business processes, and expanding analytical workloads while preserving reliable operations. Scalable cloud computing architectures offer elastic resources and reusable services, but infrastructure relocation alone does not demonstrate digital transformation. This structured narrative review examines how cloud architectural choices interact with enterprise processes, data management, and organizational governance. Peer-reviewed research on transformation, migration, distributed systems, integration, and cloud platforms is synthesized with authoritative security guidance. The analysis distinguishes resource elasticity, application scalability, and organizational capacity to operate an evolving system. The literature identifies complementary opportunities in modular deployment, differentiated data services, automated operations, and shared platform capabilities. It also reveals tradeoffs involving consistency, dependency coordination, security boundaries, and cost accountability. No architecture is shown to deliver superior enterprise outcomes across all contexts. The paper proposes an unvalidated capability-to-outcome framework connecting business requirements, bounded architectural change, operational acceptance, and post-migration review. Its contribution is to make the relationship between architectural mechanisms and transformation outcomes explicit and assessable. Evaluation should examine completed business processes, data correctness, recovery behavior, change effort, and cost per useful unit of service rather than resource growth alone. The framework provides a basis for enterprise planning and comparative research without claiming implementation results, guaranteed savings, or empirically validated causal effects.

detail.abstract: Maintenance decisions in manufacturing are commonly expressed as choices between corrective, scheduled preventive and condition-based policies. Such categories describe intervention triggers but do not establish the condition achieved after intervention. This paper examines how imperfect restoration changes policy selection when finance, staffing, competence and production access are constrained. A focused critical narrative review integrates repairable-system theory, maintenance optimisation, selective maintenance, condition monitoring and organisational research. No original dataset, experiment or numerical optimisation is reported. The analytical contribution is a restoration-sensitive decision rule that separates policy eligibility from preference and links each intervention to a feasible restoration level, resource demand and subsequent reliability exposure. A virtual-age representation clarifies why repeated partial repairs can preserve accumulated deterioration, while a separate allowance for maintenance-induced defects prevents restoration quality from being confused with intervention timing. Three propositions follow: a policy preferred under perfect restoration can lose its advantage when feasible repair effectiveness is considered; condition information has operational value only when action can occur within the available warning interval; and coordinated restoration can outperform indiscriminate task completion when specialist labour and outage windows are shared. These are conditional analytical propositions, not measured improvements. The paper provides comparative tables, original conceptual figures and a practical evidence register for evaluating policy choices across successive production periods. Its principal implication is that maintenance selection should compare executable combinations of timing and restoration depth rather than assign a single strategy label to an entire asset..

detail.abstract: Robots driven by artificial intelligence now fail in public: robotaxis block ambulances, surgical instruments break inside patients and humanoid robots lose control at exhibitions. What society learns about these failures depends on which incident regime records them. This article compares three regimes for embodied AI between 2021 and 2026: the mandatory crashreporting order of the US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (8,135 incidents involving automated driving systems or Level 2 driver assistance), the Food and Drug Administration's adverse-event register for computer-assisted surgical systems (127,627 reports since 2015) and the media-derived AI Incident Database (1,734 incidents). Fifty-four road-vehicle incidents in the media-derived database were hand-coded and linked to mandatory reports. Twenty of the 21 US crashes in the media-derived database were also reported to the regulator, but only 21 of 8,135 mandatorily reported incidents (0.26%) reached the mediaderived database. Contrary to the pre-specified expectation, media visibility rose with severity: 3.1% of fatal or serious incidents against 0.37% of the rest (odds ratio 8.7; Fisher exact p < 0.001), a gradient that keeps its direction across nine robustness checks. Almost half of the media-recorded US events (19 of 40) were operational failures without a crash, which a crashtriggered order cannot capture by design. In the surgical register, a fourfold rise in malfunction reports in 2025 is concentrated in two wear-related problem codes filed by the manufacturer, while injury reports barely changed. Humanoid robots, the most visible failures of 2026, fall under no reporting regime. Each regime sees a different class of failure, and none sees the robots now entering public space.

detail.abstract: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has become a global hub of the crypto industry. Four regulators license virtual asset firms in the UAE. A firm can choose between these regulators, and the law charges each with developing its market, conditions that are widely expected to push standards down. Yet the UAE's rules have received little academic attention, and the work that exists has described the regulators more than it has measured their rules. This article compares the four regimes with the European Union's Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCAR) and tracks how each has changed over time. It finds that, on most requirements, even the least demanding UAE regime is at least as demanding as MiCAR, and that the regulators have tightened their rules more than twice as often as they have loosened them. It argues that the description of the UAE as a light-touch jurisdiction confuses the strategy of its regulators (speed, engagement with industry and frequent revision) with the stringency of their rules. The UAE thus shows that a regulator charged with developing its market can be fast and accessible without lowering its standards.

detail.abstract: This article develops a formal notion of exchange equilibrium inspired by Edgeworth's analysis of bilateral exchange [Edgeworth, 1881]. We consider a pure exchange economy in which trade occurs through pairwise agreements between consumers. Each pair of consumers selects a feasible exchange from an Edgeworth set, while each individual retains the right to reject exchanges involving him or her. The equilibrium concept therefore combines bilateral efficiency with voluntary participation and coordination across multiple exchanges. The article formalizes the exchange environment by specifying the commodity space, the set of consumers, the feasible exchange correspondences for each pair, and the induced allocations generated by networks of bilateral trades. An exchange equilibrium is defined as a profile of pairwise exchanges satisfying feasibility, pairwise Pareto efficiency, voluntary participation, and stability against blocking deviations by any consumer pair. An existence theorem is then established for the special case of one-to-one matching economies with strict preferences. Using the Gale-Shapley deferred acceptance algorithm [Gale and Shapley, 1962], it is shown that a stable exchange equilibrium exists whenever the economy is bipartite and consumers rank potential trading partners according to the utility obtainable from feasible bilateral exchanges. The proof clarifies the relationship between exchange equilibrium and the classical theory of stable matchings. The framework connects cooperative exchange theory, Edgeworth box analysis, and matching theory. It also illustrates how decentralized bilateral agreements can generate globally stable allocations without requiring a centralized price system.

detail.abstract: The rapid expansion of data centers supporting artificial intelligence (AI) has sparked growing debate over their impacts on local communities. Concerns about pollution and health risks suggest that nearby hospitals may face greater demand. At the same time, data center development brings substantial investment that may improve local socioeconomic conditions and the availability of healthcare. We examine how large data center openings affect nearby hospitals and local healthcare markets, combining U.S. data on hospital operations and nonhospital providers over 2013-2024 in a staggered difference-indifferences (DiD) design. We find that emergency department (ED) visits at nearby hospitals decline by 6.7% following large data center openings, with effects diminishing over distance. In contrast, inpatient utilization and service performance remain relatively stable. Decomposing such decline suggests approximately 85% of the effect can be attributed to reduced county-level ED visits per resident rather than population changes or patient redistribution across those hospitals. We further document growth in physician offices and residential-care facilities, suggesting that greater nonhospital care availability may contribute to the decline in ED demand. The volume reduction is accompanied by financial consequences as nearby hospitals experience a 5.1% reduction in net patient revenue without corresponding reductions in staffing or inpatient workload. Together, our study broadens the debate on data center by providing new evidence on how such development reshapes local healthcare markets, with spillover effects on nearby hospitals. Our findings offer policymakers a more comprehensive perspective for evaluating data center projects and inform hospital managers on demand forecasting and operational planning.

detail.abstract: In May 2026, a hantavirus outbreak aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship triggered public alarm disproportionate to its actual scale, despite the rapid diagnosis, clear WHO and ECDC guidance, and swift containment within three months. This commentary asks why outbreaks that health authorities handle correctly can still produce pandemic-level panic. Drawing on media framing research and the Hondius case itself, there seem to be two forces at work. One is news coverage that foregrounds alarming questions while burying expert reassurances. The second one is that post-pandemic public has learnt to distrust reassurance after Covid, when authorities failed to convey that guidance would evolve. This piece contends that clear, accurate and timely statements from health authorities are no longer sufficient on their own and proposes three practices going forward. Recommendations involve naming and directly addressing alarming narratives early, treating community trust as infrastructure built before a crisis rather than during one, and engaging with social media conversations directly rather than relying solely on content removal. Since it was small and well controlled, this outbreak offers a low-cost opportunity to test these practices before a larger outbreak makes the same communication gap far more costly.

detail.abstract: Chronic musculoskeletal pain is one of the commonest reasons people seek physiotherapy, and clinicians are routinely asked whether hands on treatment or active exercise is the better choice. This narrative comparative review, written in 2025, examines what published evidence from 2019 to 2025 says about manual therapy and exercise therapy for persistent musculoskeletal pain. It outlines the burden and mechanisms of chronic pain, the principles behind each approach, and a transparent framework for weighing the evidence. It then considers findings for chronic low back pain, chronic neck pain, knee osteoarthritis and shoulder pain. Across these conditions, exercise therapy has the more consistent support as a foundation of care, with benefits for pain and function that are usually modest but dependable. Manual therapy tends to produce similar or slightly smaller effects when used alone, with short term relief that is helpful for some patients and an apparent added benefit when combined with exercise. Differences between the two are often small, and individual response varies widely. The review concludes that treatment should be built around the patient, with exercise as the backbone and manual therapy used selectively as an adjunct, and it identifies gaps that future trials should address.

detail.abstract: Universities, funders and governments all ask a version of the same question: did this research make a difference? Answering it is harder than it sounds. This review sets out why research impact deserves systematic measurement, which factors decide whether a measurement can be trusted, which tools are now available, and which approaches are likely to shape the next decade. It is a critical narrative review built on foundational policy statements and methodological studies, supplemented by recent evidence on data infrastructure, assessment reform, disruption indicators and AI-assisted evaluation. Reported figures were checked against the original papers, preprints or organisational pages wherever possible. Four themes emerge. First, impact is plural: scholarly, societal, economic, policy and cultural effects follow different pathways and clocks, so no single number can stand for all of them. Second, the reliability of any indicator rests on a handful of choices that are often made silently, namely the data source, the field baseline, the time window and the unit of analysis. Third, the toolbox has widened from citation counts and journal scores to open scholarly graphs, altmetrics, network-based disruption measures, narrative case studies and, most recently, large language models, each with documented strengths and blind spots. Fourth, the reform movement behind DORA, the Leiden Manifesto and CoARA has grown from a declaration into a coalition of more than 800 member organisations. We close with a layered framework that combines open data, multiple signals, AI-assisted screening under human oversight, and narrative context, all governed by equity and transparency principles.

detail.abstract: Stocks in which TEFAS funds held at least 1% of shares outstanding were more likely to hit the daily price floor (limit-down) during the September 2026 fund-liquidation crisis, and they stayed there longer. On 17 September 2026 the Capital Markets Board (SPK) halted trading in the funds of seven portfolio management companies and ordered their liquidation. Using point-in-time fund holdings from KAP Portfolio Distribution Reports (31 July 2026) for 545 Borsa Istanbul stocks, I find that a fund stake of at least 1% is associated with an 18.6 percentage point higher share of limit-down days between 31 August and 18 September and a cumulative abnormal return about 0.25 log points lower (sector-clustered wild-bootstrap p ≤ 0.001). Among the 99 stocks that closed limit-down on 17 September, the median limit-down streak is 10 trading days for stocks with a fund stake of at least 1% and 3 days for the rest (log-rank p = 1.4e-7). The effect is on the extensive margin: the linear dose of the fund stake is weak. It survives controls for new and pre-existing trading restrictions, the Pay Tebliği m.27 exit limits, free float, and sector effects, and it does not reverse after liquidation begins or after payment announcements. The exposed group had already drifted 4.9 points lower in August, about one-eighth of the gap that opens between 31 August and 18 September (t = −1.7). Results are not uniform across managers, whose subsamples are too small for inference, and cannot be separated from enforcement news on 22-23 September. This paper makes no claim about the conduct of any party and is not evidence of any party's conduct; the investigation is ongoing.

detail.abstract: Modern manufacturing enterprises universally adopt common components, standard modules, and shared production equipment to achieve economies of scale. However, this resource sharing fundamentally restructures the physical connectivity of the enterprise: horizontal "one-to-many" exclusive allocation and vertical "multi-material kitting" bottleneck constraints intertwine, casting the entire organization into an entangled, network-wide coupled state. For decades, industry and academia have attributed planning failures and cross-functional KPI conflicts to inaccurate forecasting, poor master data quality, or organizational silos, seeking to resolve these frictions through frequent Sales and Operations Planning (S&OP) meetings and localized optimization heuristics. Applying Occam's razor to strip away all external disturbances, this paper discovers and proves the governing objective law of shared-resource networks: The Law of Sequencing Coupling. Our derivation demonstrates that even under idealized, noise-free conditions-where demand forecasts are 100% deterministic, master data is 100% clean, constraints are fully mapped, and all organizational friction is eliminated-as long as an enterprise shares resources to pursue economies of scale, any action that sequentially allocates and exclusively locks inventory based on static business priorities inevitably causes late-kitting, high-priority demands to monopolize early on-hand stock whenever business priority and physical kitting dates invert. This allocation cascades across the shared network to block the fulfillment of early-kitting demands, deterministically (100%) generating a spatiotemporal cross-mismatch where "early demands starve waiting for late arrivals, while late demands sit idle hoarding early stock." This phenomenon occurs universally across strategic, tactical, and operational S&OP horizons, proving that cross-functional KPI conflicts are physical couplings rather than mere differences in stance. Arbitrary manual expediting and priority overrides in S&OP meetings do not resolve this coupling; instead, they trigger network-wide vector cancellation, hemorrhaging the enterprise's Return on Invested Capital (ROIC). Finally, this paper presents an orthogonal governance architecture that resolves cross-mismatch without abandoning economies of scale: implementing soft allocation concessions that preserve delivery commitments, and orthogonally decoupling additive material flows from time-exclusive discrete machine capacity. Rooted in this orthogonal governance mechanism, the Integrated Planning Solution (IPS) of Lenovo Group closed the high-frequency "plan-execute-feedback" loop, achieving an across-the-board leap in operational KPIs and capital returns across 18 consecutive years of rigorous industrial practice (2008-2026).

detail.abstract: Large retail chains must tailor assortment and pricing decisions to local customer preferences, yet even retailers with extensive sales records often have limited data for estimating demand at the store or local market level, particularly in product categories with short selling windows. Local estimation-fitting a demand model for each store on its own-can therefore be unreliable, while pooling data across stores improves estimation precision at the cost of ignoring local demand heterogeneity. We study how retailers can balance these competing effects through transfer learning under a multinomial logit (MNL) demand model. We propose a shrinkage estimator that combines store-specific demand estimates with information pooled from other stores. Unlike the linear or quadratic settings underlying much of the existing theoretical literature on information transfer in operations, the nonlinear MNL likelihood does not admit a straightforward bias-variance decomposition. By exploiting its self-concordant-like properties, we establish finite-sample performance guarantees that characterize when information transfer improves demand estimation and how the appropriate degree of shrinkage depends on local sample size, feature dimensionality, and cross-store heterogeneity. We further derive regret bounds for downstream assortment and pricing decisions. Numerical experiments demonstrate the operational benefits of shrinkage across different data environments. An empirical study using data from several hundred stores of a European apparel retailer shows that shrinkage improves out-of-sample product prioritization and revenue capture relative to both local estimation and full pooling. Our findings demonstrate how retailers can leverage information across their store networks to improve revenue management decisions while preserving local demand differences.

detail.abstract: This paper considers the Bayesian top-k identification problem, wherein a decision maker is tasked with selecting k items from a pool of items of unknown quality. To assess the items, the decision maker adaptively allocates a fixed sampling budget, where each sample of an item yields a noisy observation of its quality, with the objective of minimizing the expected opportunity cost of the selected set. We propose an approach that allocates each batch of samples by minimizing a surrogate objective derived from an upper bound on the expected opportunity cost. The approach is general: samples can be allocated in batches, the selection size k is arbitrary, and it applies to many sampling distributions. It is also simple and intuitive. We prove that the method's posterior expected opportunity cost decays at an exponential rate of at least half the best rate achievable by any sampling rule. In simulations across a wide range of settings, the method is competitive with, and often improves upon, the best existing algorithm in each setting.

detail.abstract: This paper considers a decision-maker tasked with identifying the 𝑘 best items from a large pool of candidates, such as job applicants, LLMs, award nominees, or new product ideas. The decision-maker learns about the items' quality by soliciting human evaluations. Each evaluation can be costly, so the decision-maker aims to use the limited evaluation budget efficiently by allocating evaluations adaptively. A key consideration is the form of evaluation to solicit, which should be something evaluators are comfortable providing. Two popular forms are ratings and pairwise comparisons, and we allow for both, as they may be especially useful in combination given the limited budget. Ratings can be used early on to get a coarse picture of which items are good and which are not. As that picture forms, comparisons can refine the ordering of the good items, narrowing in on the ultimate top-𝑘 selection. To solve the allocation problem, we develop an adaptive algorithm built from two allocation policies. The first, our primary contribution, is based on a surrogate objective that is naturally forward-looking, valuing evaluations that help inform what to evaluate in future rounds, not just those that directly improve the selection decision. The decision rule is interpretable, and we prove that it is asymptotically consistent. Late in the evaluation process, when being forward-looking is less productive, we construct a myopic policy and a criterion for switching to it. In simulation, the method gives insight into how to combine these two types of evaluations, and beats the (limited) existing benchmarks.

detail.abstract: Predictive maintenance uses sensor data and failure-prediction models to replace fixedinterval or run-to-failure servicing of industrial equipment. The engineering case for it is well established. The management question is less studied: once a manufacturer decides to monitor its machines, should it build the capability in-house, subscribe to a vendor platform, or contract a condition-monitoring service provider? We develop a sourcing model in which annual net benefit depends on the number of critical machines, the cost of unplanned downtime, the loaded cost of engineering labour, and the effective cost of capital, scaled by a capital-availability index. We apply it to stylized manufacturers in Moldova and Romania. Four results follow. First, in-house development pays only above about 8 critical machines in Moldova and 4 in Romania, and leads every other route only above about 29 and 14 machines respectively. Second, contracted condition monitoring is the best route for small and medium-small fleets in both countries. Third, the smallest Moldovan fleets are best served by a vendor platform, while Romanian ones already favour a contractor. Fourth, raising Moldova's capital-availability index to the Romanian level would halve the in-house threshold, from about 29 to about 14 machines. The binding constraint on engineering self-reliance in these economies therefore appears to be capital, not technical skill.

detail.abstract: We explore whether interlocking directorates facilitate technology exclusion, whereby a licensing relationship between connected firms restricts other downstream peers' access to the licensed technology. We find that firms connected through board overlap are more likely to enter into licensing agreements and that, following these agreements, licensors reduce further licensing to other firms that build on the technology. Consistent with exclusion, these downstream peers file fewer patent applications than peers of comparable agreements without board overlap, while their R&D spending is unchanged. The decline is concentrated in the technology area covered by the agreement rather than affected peers' other technology areas. We find that the effects are more pronounced for affected peers that compete with the licensee in the product markets, rely on the licensor's technology, or have less financial flexibility. Affected peers also produce less original, less specific, and less valuable patents and delay disclosing their innovation. We further find that interlock-driven agreements are structured to promote exclusivity and long-term collaboration and compensate licensors through fixed and guaranteed payments.

detail.abstract: Assessments of physical security systems often report a single result that blends three different questions: whether each control passed its test, whether a capable responder can interrupt an adversary in time, and who has accepted the loss that remains. This paper presents the Facility Security System Framework, a three-gate method that keeps those answers as separate, recorded results. The framework rests on three rules. The first rule keeps the interruption judgment on its own timeliness calculation, so that a facility whose controls all pass inspection still receives a measured judgment. The second rule leaves the grade blank whenever an element of that calculation is missing in the current cycle, and names the missing element. The third rule keeps the owner's acceptance of the owner's own loss on one line and harm to third parties on a separate line that closes only on evidence that the harm has ceased. The paper places the framework beside the timely-detection model of physical protection evaluation, ISO 31000, ISO 22340, ANSI/ASIS PAP.1, and published United States federal guidance; shows that its judgment is the deterministic case of the EASI model; describes its assessment cycle, roles, records, five hierarchical layers, and six indicators; sets out an operational sequence across three facility classes; and illustrates it with worked and hypothetical examples at a telecommunications exchange, a data center, and a multi-site portfolio. The framework draws on the author's commissioning work at telephone exchanges and data centers in the United Arab Emirates from 2015 to 2020.

detail.abstract: Climate variability is changing the way poultry is reared in Nigeria, yet little is known about how farmers in Okpe see it and respond to it. This study assessed poultry farmers' perception and adaptation to climate variability in Orerokpe Community, Okpe Local Government Area, Delta State. A descriptive survey was carried out among 100 purposively selected poultry farmers, and the data were analysed with frequencies, means, Pearson correlation and the ttest. Farmers agreed that climate variability is real (grand mean = 4.08), reporting rising temperature (89.0%), irregular rainfall (70.0%) and flooding (54.0%). Perception, flood experience and climate information were each significantly related to adaptation. High feed cost, lack of funds and power failure were the main constraints. The study recommends better climate information, credit, drainage and power support.

detail.abstract: This paper provides archival and experimental evidence that equity market feedback influences firms' environmental behavior. Following the publication of U.S. Reports on Carcinogens, firms using newly identified carcinogens that experience particularly negative stock-price reactions reduce toxic waste more, especially when their worker exposure is high. Cross-sectional tests show stronger effects where market signals are likely to be more informative, and peer-firm evidence suggests that firms also learn from affected firms' stock-price reactions. We complement the archival evidence with an information provision experiment using participants with managerial experience in TRI-reporting industries. Participants assigned randomly to a negative stock-market signal are more likely to state that they would undertake costly toxic-release reductions and abatement. Overall, while existing research emphasizes divestment and engagement, this paper highlights an additional mechanism through which financial markets shape corporate responsibility: prices convey information that managers use to adjust environmental practices.

detail.abstract: We examine how political polarization affects banks' liquidity transformation using quarterly data on U.S. commercial banks from 2001 to 2024. We find that a onestandard-deviation increase in partisan conflict lowers liquidity creation by 0.4% of its sample mean and raises liquidity hoarding by 2-3%, with total hoarding rising 8.5% from average to peak polarization. Measured against total assets, hoarding rises three to four times as much as creation falls, indicating that banks respond mainly through precautionary self-insurance. Lower loan-to-deposit ratios and higher liquid-asset and stable-funding ratios corroborate this interpretation. We identify two mechanisms. First, an instrumental-variable analysis shows that policy uncertainty is an important channel through which polarization affects banks' liquidity decisions. Second, we document a delayed-stabilization channel, whereby expectations of slower or less credible public intervention intensify precautionary hoarding. The effects are strongest among smaller banks and banks more reliant on uninsured deposits, and they intensify during presidential elections and recessions. Our findings identify political polarization as an economically meaningful determinant of bank liquidity management, with implications for financial stability and macroprudential supervision.
