detail.abstract: Agency ratings are revised infrequently, whereas secondary-market spreads are repriced daily. We develop an estimator that maps traded corporate-bond spreads into an ordinal credit scale while purging the term premium, and we show why the conventional purge fails. In a daily panel of 70,276 AN-BIMA indicative rates on 1,222 Brazilian debentures from 372 issuers (2026Q1), the slope of spreads on duration among floating-rate (DI+) bonds is-13.3 bp per year in the cross-section but +10.0 bp (issuerclustered s.e. 2.7) within issuer and date-a sign reversal that replicates the maturity-selection bias of Helwege and Turner (1999) in an emerging market. Our K-Curves estimator gives each latent class a Nelson-Siegel credit curve, which we derive from a mean-reverting reduced-form default intensity; it identifies levels from the cross-section and slopes exclusively from within-issuer variation, under a noncrossing restriction that we prove reduces to an endpoint condition. Among inflation-linked bonds, a conventional single-curve adjustment raises the within-issuer correlation between credit label and duration to +0.51; our labels lower it to-0.04. The scale does not forecast spread volatility better than raw spreads, and its ordering of absolute volatility is largely mechanical: its contribution is to measurement, not prediction. Among agency-AAA DI+ bonds, those the scale places below its two best classes exhibit a median future spread volatility of 149.8 bp against 22.0 bp (issuer-bootstrap 95% interval for the difference [19.1, 1,691.1]).

detail.abstract: I introduce an indefinitely repeated prisoner's dilemma in which the continuation probability depends on how many players cooperate. Theoretically, the payoff from mutual cooperation and the continuation probability it induces act as substitutes in sustaining cooperative equilibria. I test this in a laboratory experiment with a 2×2 between-subjects design that independently varies these two parameters. Three results emerge. First, an increase in the continuation probability associated with joint cooperation promotes cooperation only when it makes cooperation sustainable in equilibrium. Second, early in the experiment, payoff incentives raise cooperation more than theoretically equivalent continuation incentives; this asymmetry disappears with experience. Third, estimated strategies display substitutability between the two forces once treatments are matched on strategic uncertainty.

detail.abstract:
This article examines the mechanisms of behavioral convergence among economic agents by extending traditional frameworks based on preference adaptation, network effects, or institutional constraints. It introduces the concept of the “Constrained Environment,” defined as a dissipative structure that endogenously reduces the space of sustainable choices. Within this framework, convergence can emerge independently of attraction toward an optimal option or selection through direct elimination, as a result of continuous mechanical attrition exerted by the environment on trajectories that deviate from its structural support.
Using topological modeling and a stochastic optimization program, this work shows that the deterioration of an agent’s autonomy capital leads to a progressive contraction of the set of viable choices. The analysis characterizes a partition of phase space into three dynamic regimes (Alignment, Resistance, and Escape) and demonstrates that, as the ruin threshold approaches, the agent’s behavioral sensitivity diverges, leading it almost surely to conform to the environment’s non-dissipative core to ensure its survival.
Applied to microeconomic informality traps and macroeconomic development blockages, this model provides a unified analytical framework. It highlights the limitations of public policies based on simple marginal incentives (prices, taxes, subsidies) for agents in the resistance regime, and emphasizes the value of interventions based on direct injections of autonomy capital or meta-transitions that restructure the space of constraints itself.

detail.abstract: Conventional statistical physics and quantum mechanics typically evaluate the probability of macroscopic configurations from an external, third-person perspective, dismissing the extreme improbability of the chain of events leading to a specific observer as a retrospective probability fallacy. This paper demonstrates that such an approach constitutes a methodological and physical fallacy by omitting a primary empirical parameter: the existence and first-person conscious experience of the observer (the reader) against an overwhelming set of inert timelines ("dead timelines"). By calculating the cumulative probability of the discrete set of configuration events from the Last Universal Common Ancestor (LUCA, approximately 4,000 million years ago) down to the exact line of events terminating in the reader, we obtain probabilities on the order of 𝑃 ≈ 10-575,000,000 (51,458.46 σ) over the last 205 million years, and 𝑃 ≈ 10-23,740,000,000 (330,645.93 σ) since LUCA. Postulating a single universe governed by stochastic wave-function collapse requires accepting an irrational statistical anomaly. As a solution of maximum axiomatic parsimony, a physical and informational model is developed based exclusively on spacetime relativity, Dirac's relativistic quantum mechanics, and Everett's relative state formulation. A block universe of at least five dimensions is proposed in which, alongside ordinary spatial coordinates (𝑋, 𝑌, 𝑍), two additional spatial axes emerge: ana-kata (the entropic vector driven by quantum entanglement, subjectively perceived as time) and superana-superkata (the axis along which quantum branching occurs). Finally, it is shown that the stability of classical laws and the absence of macroscopic quantum anomalies are the direct result of pure combinatorial branch entropy (where inconceivably more microstates exist within normal macrostates than within abnormal ones) combined with the anthropic and Copernican principles.

detail.abstract: Courts and administrative bodies usually treat exclusion as an event: a decision, a decision-maker, a motive. A recurring observation across constitutional systems is that exclusion often appears instead as a pattern produced by sequences of facially independent decisions, and that the pattern looks structurally similar at the level of a single proceeding, an institutional pipeline, and a whole legal system. This article examines whether that recurrence is analytically defensible and what it implies for adjudication. It develops the hypothesis that, where institutions apply sequential, locally rational filters to individuated cases, exclusion tends to reproduce a similar structure across scales, and that doctrines demanding proof at a single scale are structurally unable to register it. The method is doctrinal, comparative and theoretical; no original empirical study is claimed. Drawing on complexity theory, the sociology of cumulative advantage, intersectionality scholarship and the study of street-level administration, the article analyses McCleskey v. Kemp (United States), ADPF 347 (Brazil), judgment T-025 of 2004 and its follow-up orders (Colombia), and Grootboom (South Africa). The analysis suggests that individuated-proof doctrines and systemic remedies each operate at one scale and leave cross-scale recurrence partly unaddressed, and that the Colombian follow-up orders illustrate recurrence inside remediation itself. The contribution is an operational conception of scale recurrence, a doctrinal explanation of why single-scale adjudication cannot see it, and a bounded set of institutional safeguards: stage-wise attrition records, record-based burden shifting at the institutional level, and remedies designed against generative mechanisms. The article states conditions that would falsify the hypothesis and explains why recurrence, even if confirmed, would limit but not defeat the possibility of justice. detail.abstract: This paper synthesises the global hedonic housing literature from 1970 to 2026 with a reproducible pipeline: 103,011 records identified from Semantic Scholar, Crossref, arXiv and OpenAlex, 56,727 unique records screened by rules and by independent agents following a PRISMA-style protocol, 2,249 hedonic studies included at stage one, 501 open-access full texts retrieved, and 242 eligible studies from 55 countries extracted into 18,831 coefficient rows with a validated double-extraction sample. Coefficients are harmonised into percentage premiums, semi-elasticities per common unit and elasticities, and pooled with random-effects, three-level and cluster-robust models, with publication-selection diagnostics, Bayesian and machine-learning cross-checks. The structural core of the hedonic model is global: the elasticity of price to living area is 0.65, a bathroom adds 5.91 percent, a year of age subtracts-0.24 percent and a kilometre from the centre-3.08 percent, with similar means across continents and decades. Signature amenities carry premiums between four and eleven percent and a waterfront location 32.50 percent. Every implicit price is heterogeneous beyond sampling error, prediction intervals span zero for most characteristics, and observable study features, including spatial estimators, explain little of the heterogeneity. Funnel asymmetry is widespread but not interpretable as selection alone. Machine-learning models predict better than hedonic benchmarks in most of the forty retrievable comparisons, while AI-derived text and image features add modest accuracy and some interpretable characteristics. The synthesis extends Sirmans et al. (2005, 2006) in coverage, harmonisation, inference and scope, and is bounded by the open-access retrieval rate that it documents.

detail.abstract: This paper compares econometric and machine-learning approaches to hedonic housing valuation on 788,842 active Zillow listings covering all 50 U.S. states and the District of Columbia, and asks how much of the machine-learning advantage survives when models must price homes in markets they have not seen. A semi-log OLS model with 62 regressors (𝑅 2 = 0.634) yields listing-price gradients consistent with the hedonic literature; ZIP3 fixed effects raise out-of-sample 𝑅 2 to 0.725 and residual Moran's 𝐼 = 0.27 shows strong spatial dependence. Allowing for that dependence matters: cluster-robust standard errors are, on median, 8 (ZIP3) to 12 (state) times the HC3 errors, and only 33 of 63 coefficients remain significant under state clustering. State-by-state estimation shows that the pooled coefficients average markedly different local price functions (living-area elasticities from 0.06 to 1.15) and that a fully interacted model gains 6.1 points of out-of-sample 𝑅 2 over state fixed effects. Quantile regression reveals distributional heterogeneity, with paired cluster-bootstrap Wald tests rejecting equality of the 10th-and 90th-percentile coefficients for 10 of 13 key attributes. XGBoost reaches 𝑅 2 = 0.833 under random validation but 0.425 under a ten-state holdout and a median of 0.653 across 51 leave-one-state-out models; once 0.6% of corrupt records are removed, OLS is as accurate out of state (0.539) as the best tree ensemble. The gap is traced to the prediction of market price levels rather than within-market structure (within-state 𝑅 2 = 0.62), to region dummies and to "neighbourhood" variables that are state-median imputations for 93% of listings, and to boosting capacity: held-out-state accuracy peaks after 75 rounds and declines thereafter while within-training accuracy keeps rising. SHAP rankings are stable across ensembles (𝜌 > 0.89), and the third-ranked feature is a state identifier. A coding error that set ln(lot) to zero for 16.5% of listings is corrected (lot elasticity 0.095, not 0.018). Estimates are interpreted throughout as conditional associations in asking prices, not willingness-to-pay parameters.

detail.abstract: Building maintenance accounts for a substantial proportion of carbon emissions and cost, highlighting the importance of efficient maintenance strategies. In response, predictive maintenance has emerged as a data-driven approach to improve asset performance, reduce failures, and support sustainability objectives. However, the effectiveness of this data-driven approach depends heavily on the availability and quality of integrated data from multiple building systems. There are numerous studies on data challenges and requirements for predictive maintenance in buildings, yet there is no synthesised study. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the status quo of data requirements and data challenges for enabling predictive maintenance in buildings with a focus on achieving cost-carbon optimisation. The study adopted a systematic literature review approach using the Scopus and Web of Science databases. From an initial pool of 1,289 sources, the study selected 63 papers for analysis. Based on these papers, the study identified 33 data challenges and 27 data requirements. The findings demonstrate that predictive maintenance requires high-resolution, high-frequency, real-time, continuous, longitudinal, and multi-domain data streams to support reliable decision-making. The findings also demonstrate that cost-carbon optimisation depends on data quality and availability, as inaccurate predictions can result in premature maintenance, delayed interventions, avoidable carbon emissions, and additional lifecycle cost. Based on these findings, the study proposed a hierarchy of data constraints that connects data conditions, predictive maintenance performance, and cost-carbon outcomes. Accordingly, the study contributes to research by structuring the relationship between data challenges, data requirements, predictive maintenance, and cost-carbon optimisation. The study further supports industry by clarifying critical data gaps that hinder implementation, and contributes to society by allowing more efficient, carbon-cost optimised management of building assets.

detail.abstract: This report discusses the performance management of PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BRI) based on an analysis of the 2025 performance report. The discussion covers BRI's business profile and focus, the development of financial indicators, human resource management, the performance management system, competency and career development, the impact of HR management on business performance, sustainability through Green Human Resource Management (GHRM), and a SWOT analysis. In 2025, BRI demonstrated business volume growth, reflected in an increase in total assets to Rp2,135 trillion, loans and financing to Rp1,521 trillion, and third-party funds to Rp1,467 trillion. However, this growth was accompanied by pressure on profitability and efficiency, as evidenced by a decline in net income to Rp57.1 trillion, ROA to 2.74%, NIM to 6.47%, and an increase in CIR to 42.55%. On the HR front, BRI strengthened its talent pipeline, competencies, and succession planning through various development programs. Overall, BRI's performance management system has been integrated to encompass KPIs, behavioral assessments, development, and talent management, although there are still areas for improvement, such as linking individual performance to business efficiency, measuring training ROI, integrating GHRM into formal KPIs, and controlling HR costs.

detail.abstract: We study whether corporate risk disclosure is informative about anticipated tail risk and how that information is reflected in asset prices. From the narrative risk factor sections of 10-K filings, we build a text-based, firm-level measure of tail-risk disclosure and show that it captures independently measured tail-risk exposure. Firms with more extensive disclosure earn higher expected returns, consistent with investors demanding compensation for known downside exposures. Yet when disclosed risks materialize, these firms experience smaller and less persistent price declines than comparable non-disclosers, indicating that disclosure shifts adjustment from abrupt ex post repricing toward gradual ex ante pricing. We confirm this timing mechanism in two complementary event settings. When a previously disclosed risk materializes, prior disclosers experience smaller abnormal losses. When the perceived materiality of an existing risk increases without new firm-level information, firms that had disclosed the exposure are repriced first. The results establish risk disclosure as a measure of anticipated tail risk and show that transparent communication shapes when downside risk enters prices

Gluons Shop Limited has developed an innovative, AI-powered Smart Inventory Management System designed to digitally integrate retailers, distributors, manufacturers, and government authorities through a single, interconnected platform.

detail.abstract: Dumping overburden and waste rock is routine in opencast mining, but it brings heavy vehicles, dozers, changing ground, and steep faces together in one work area. Water can soften a platform, a crest can deteriorate, and a small change in conditions can leave a truck with little room to recover. This technical review brings together Indian research, Directorate General of Mines Safety (DGMS) guidance, international technical material, and selected fatalincident summaries from DGMS SANKET coal and non-coal reports. It develops a task-based hazard assessment, an illustrative bow-tie, and a critical-barrier register, then applies the framework retrospectively to eight selected SANKET dumper and tipper cases. The cases illustrate several pathways: edge overrun at a dump, use of a nondesignated point, loss of control on a haul road, reversing into a person, and rollover during raised-body unloading. They are purposively selected examples, not a complete census or exposure-adjusted analysis. The proposed system is designed to link dump design and foundations with drainage, monitoring, traffic management, equipment readiness, supervision, and emergency response. Where the approved design permits, short dumping with controlled dozer placement is preferred because it can keep loaded trucks farther from the crest; truck-dozer interaction and the dozer push limit still require control. Direct end-dumping requires documented, site-specific assessment and written authorisation. Cracks, settlement, slumping, seepage, drainage failure, damaged edge protection, abnormal vehicle response, monitoring warnings, poor visibility, or loss of communication call for work to stop and the area to be reassessed. The case application shows how the framework can organise control decisions; it does not establish that the framework prevents accidents. The paper offers a basis for mine-specific procedures, not a universal design standard or a substitute for statutory duties and approved engineering.

detail.abstract: In order to maintain organizational cohesion that supports effective functioning in an educational institution, effective conflict resolution is needed. Despite growing research on conflict management in educational organizations, there exists limited empirical evidence examining different approaches, including the mediating role of organizational cohesion explaining the relationship between conflict-resolution approaches and institutional effectiveness in Nigerian public secondary schools. This study therefore examined the relationship between conflict resolution approaches, organizational cohesion, and institutional effectiveness in public secondary schools in Cross River State, Nigeria. Specifically, it investigated the relationship between conflict resolution approaches and organizational cohesion and examined the mediating role of organizational cohesion. The study adopted a correlational research design. While the target population comprised 5,104 (principals, vice-principals, and teachers) from 274 public secondary schools in Cross River State, Nigeria, from which a sample of 400 respondents was selected using a multistage sampling procedure. Data were collected using structured questionnaires and analyzed using Pearson Product-Moment Correlation, Multiple Linear Regression, and Hayes’ PROCESS Macro Model 4 with 5,000 bootstrap samples. From the findings it was revealed that conflict resolution approaches were positively associated with organizational cohesion (r = .684, p < .001). The five conflict-resolution dimensions jointly explained 35.5% of the variance in institutional effectiveness (R² = .355, p < .001). Organizational cohesion showed a significant indirect effect in the relationship between conflict resolution approaches and institutional effectiveness (indirect effect = .271, 95% bootstrap CI [.198, .352]). This study extends the literature on conflict management in educational organizations by empirically examining organizational cohesion as a relational mechanism associated with the relationship between conflict resolution approaches and institutional effectiveness in public secondary schools in Cross River State. The study concluded that effective conflict resolution approaches were associated with organizational cohesion and with higher institutional effectiveness. It is based on this conclusion that the study recommends, among others, that school administrators adopt collaborative conflict management practices to enhance a cohesive work environment and improve school effectiveness

detail.abstract: Public debate on artificial intelligence (AI) and humanoid robotics often centres on productivity, job displacement, and Universal Basic Income (UBI). This paper argues that a deeper risk is civilisational: advanced automation can erode human agency, responsibility, and the social expectation of contribution-what we term the False Eden condition, in which material provision is sustained while the institutional and cultural bases of participation weaken. Drawing on a crosstradition analysis of dignity (Abrahamic, Indic, and Confucian), we identify a convergent moral anthropology that links human flourishing to stewardship-disciplined responsibility for others, for the community, and for the entrusted world-rather than to passive receipt of welfare. On this basis, we advance three claims that have received limited attention in AI-and-society scholarship. First, a convergent civilisational expectation links human dignity to stewardship rather than passive provision-a moral anthropology with direct consequences for how welfare systems should be designed. Second, welfare-state design should be understood as a form of AI governance: the institutional architecture through which societies decide whether automation leads to participatory inclusion or long-term detachment. Third, UBI, while valuable as a shock absorber, is insufficient as a civilisational response unless coupled with credible structures for capability-building and socially recognised contribution. We propose Contribution-Oriented Basic Income (COBI), a modernised participation income in which conditionality is supportive rather than punitive, anchored in plural pathways-work, learning, caregiving, civic stewardship, and entrepreneurship-and accompanied by safeguards against coercion, surveillance, and algorithmic gatekeeping. Two illustrative cases-Nauru's post-resource collapse and the contrast between pre-2011 and post-2011 Hungary-ground these arguments in observable institutional dynamics and surface the trade-offs that any activation-oriented welfare architecture must confront.

detail.abstract: Choosing the estimation window changes both the amount and the historical composition of data available to a forecasting algorithm. This study compares expanding and fixed 120-observation windows for monthly US inflation using four seasonally adjusted price indexes, twelve own-history predictors, and direct oneand three-month targets. Hyperparameters are selected with chronological development forecasts ending in September 2004 and frozen for 240 common test endpoints in 2005-2024. All training labels must have matured by each forecast origin. Across eight related tasks, expanding random forest has the lowest mean RMSE ratio relative to a trailing-year mean benchmark, 0.917; expanding gradient boosting, OLS, and ridge attain 0.924, 0.934, and 0.943. Rolling estimation increases full-period RMSE in 23 of 24 primary tuned-model contrasts. However, most block-bootstrap intervals include zero, and the only 5% Holm-adjusted finding with twelve-month blocks does not survive twenty-four-month blocks. Rolling ridge improves descriptively in 2023-2024 after underperforming during 2020-2022. Window-length and fixed-penalty checks support reporting training-history sensitivity alongside algorithm comparisons. The evidence is limited to an archived revised-data snapshot and a univariate information set; it does not establish real-time performance or a universally optimal window.

detail.abstract: We develop a novel directional inflation narratives (DIN) index using large language model embeddings applied to Wall Street Journal articles from 1984 to 2024. The index captures whether inflation-related news points toward rising or declining inflation. We find that increases in DIN are followed by higher household inflation expectations and contain information about subsequent realized inflation. Using CPI announcement surprises as an instrument for daily DIN, we provide causal evidence that more inflationary narratives raise household inflation expectations. The relationship between DIN and inflation expectations is stronger when attention to inflation is high and among households with greater news exposure. Moreover, DIN helps explain forecast errors in inflation expectations and sheds light on time-varying information rigidities. Energy and labor feature prominently in inflation narratives, while the importance of other factors varies across episodes. The results are robust to concerns about LLM look-ahead bias, and the embedding-based measure consistently outperforms traditional text analysis methods. These findings show that the direction conveyed by news narratives shapes household inflation expectations and highlight the potential of LLM embeddings for extracting economically meaningful information from large-scale text.

detail.abstract: Valdos Consulting is a private firm specializing in technology and workforce strategy across public and private sectors, with extensive experience in navigating the labor market demands of industrial transitions and rapid technological change. Our applied research supports strategic planning for critical national priorities, including Defense Industrial Base scaling, domestic mineral extraction, and the development of workforce strategies for emerging sectors like quantum engineering and artificial intelligence (AI). Throughout these engagements, we have relied on the Occupational Information Network (O*NET) as the primary analytical backbone for decomposing tasks, skills, and occupational requirements. While this framework is essential for characterizing how work is performed, our analyses have revealed structural limitations introduced by expert-elicited data with substantial latency, resulting in an occupational taxonomy that often struggles to capture the rapid fluidity of modern labor markets. Furthermore, granularity suffers with over-specification in mature roles and systemic blind spots in emerging, high-stakes fields like specialized scientific research and advanced cybersecurity. An optimized content model would bridge data-driven research and actionable policy across varying use cases. In academic and labor market analytics, the framework allows researchers to mathematically model the economy as a complex network where skill proximity determines the ease of mobility and earnings potential. By treating occupations as nodes within this network, analysts can predict how technological disruptions like AI will reshape productivity and influence worker displacement. For career planning and workforce development, a modernized system offers the empirical basis for individualized navigation, helping workers identify "bridge roles" that share characteristics with current and desired occupations, minimizing retraining time and transition frictions. When applied to national policy, a data-driven content model would provide the precision necessary for characterizing AI exposure, securing talent for emerging industries, managing military-to-civilian labor transitions, and aligning immigration policies with observed labor shortages. To address current limitations, we propose a three-pronged strategy designed to transform the taxonomy from a rigid hierarchy into a dynamic, evidence-based knowledge engine. First, we advocate for the integration of low-latency data sources  to augment surveys with observed market behavior, such as large-scale job postings and resume data. Second, we recommend validation protocols that test taxonomy structures against real-world economic outcomes, such as actual wage growth and occupational transition patterns, to ensure the model reflects the realities of the labor market. Third, we propose benchmarking the content model against external, domain-specific ontologies, such as those in cybersecurity, advanced manufacturing, and clinical medicine. Throughout these stages, access to state or federal microdata such as O*NET-encoded unemployment insurance records can provide rich performance testing datasets and transparent, representative standards. Ultimately, these methodological improvements are essential to supporting national priorities. By implementing a more detailed and rapidly evolving content model, policymakers can move beyond descriptive statistics to predictive workforce planning. This level of precision is required to identify viable transition pathways for displaced workers, secure talent for the next generation of scientific and technical industries, and ensure that educational investments harmonize with real-time labor demand. Strengthening these foundations will enhance both individual career outcomes and long-term national competitiveness of the United States workforce in an increasingly volatile and technology-driven global economy.

detail.abstract: The EU Cybersecurity Reserve relies on private providers making urgent decisions across contractual, tort and data-protection regimes. This article develops an instrument-selection framework for protecting reasonable response while preserving effective redress. It connects the classification of claims with the evidence needed to assess a particular response act and the authority required to attach legal consequences to that evidence. Doctrinal analysis of EU and French law, public procurement documents and a hospital deployment hypothetical distinguishes the functions of contracts, guidance, certification and a care presumption. The principal claim concerns a third party invoking contractual breach, including applicable contractual conditions. Claims alleging an independent duty require their own legal basis. GDPR security and compensation follow a separate route. The comparison holds records and access conditions constant and varies the treatment of compliance evidence. In three stipulated variations, reasonable containment, an ignored warning and justified departure from a standard produce the same direction of care assessment under ordinary proof and the proposed rule. Qualification and challenge stages supply the rule's distinctive legal effect. Separate boundary tests address incomplete records and standards that omit material risks. The resulting framework prioritises clear authority, usable records and proportionate access. A further evidential rule requires an identified legal function, adequate safeguards and a suitable EU legal basis. This sequence supplies a practical method for deciding when responder protection calls for improved contracting and evidence arrangements, and when additional legislation merits consideration.

detail.abstract: Learned messages can leave their meaning unresolved while already determining a unique optimal action. We characterize this decision sufficiency by the common-action margin: the smallest action advantage across every interpretation consistent with public evidence. Centered value regression removes offsets irrelevant to action comparisons, complete-margin supervision learns the shared decision boundary, and conformal calibration certifies the prediction-selected margin over complete physical tasks. Correctly certified context mass rises from 63.02% to 74.81% in an independent held-out study, a gain of 11.79 percentage points. A separate seven-interface evaluation yields a 9.58-point gain over centered learning with selected-gap calibration, with positive adjusted gains over centered, ranking and SPO+ controls on ambiguous contexts. Certifying the size of this advantage reveals a second requirement: the calibration correction must lie inside a two-sided admissible interval. We derive its exact failure event, a sharp finite-catalog capacity theorem for bounded public-feature scaling, and its finite-calibration capture probability under independent, identically distributed tasks. Native warehouse counterfactuals demonstrate common optimal dispatch decisions under unresolved interpretations. Together, these results establish common-action advantage as a learnable and certifiable basis for acting before semantic identification, with a quantitative budget for retaining the decision under public cost changes.

detail.abstract: Conditional approval (CA) schemes postpone the final reimbursement decision until additional evidence about a new treatment's health-economic value is available. We study the effect of CA on pharmaceutical companies' decisions regarding how much data to collect in clinical trials and when to submit it to a healthcare payer for reimbursement. We develop a Bayesian decision-theoretic model in which a company chooses how much data to collect before and after submission, anticipating regulatory authorization, as well as the equilibrium outcomes of reimbursement negotiations with the payer. We compare the company's decisions and negotiation outcomes with and without the availability of CA. We complement our analytical results with a numerical case study calibrated to UK approval data of an oncology drug. We find that CA mostly leads to earlier submissions with less data but increases the total amount of data collected for conditionally approved treatments. Therefore, evaluating the success of CA schemes should consider their effects on both treatments that receive CA and those that do not. CA can increase the data collection burden for companies, but provides greater flexibility in data collection and submission timing, leading to a higher expected profit. The increase in profit does not necessarily come at the expense of the payer, who also receives higher net benefit in the case study. Our results highlight that the effect of CA on patient access can look different depending on whether it is measured by timing, probability, or the expected number of patients treated.

detail.abstract: Climb-phase trajectory generation is an important foundation for airspace operations management, mission planning, and simulation and wargaming. Because the performance parameters of military aircraft are largely classified, model-driven methods struggle to establish accurate physical models; meanwhile, publicly available surveillance data are scarce and the observations incomplete, so purely data-driven methods can neither adequately learn the true climb patterns nor, lacking physical constraints, avoid generating infeasible trajectories that exceed the aircraft performance envelope. To address these problems, this paper proposes PG-ClimbDiff, a physics-guided diffusion framework for climb-profile generation. Taking altitude as the independent variable, the framework represents a climb trajectory as profiles of speed and climb rate versus altitude, thereby eliminating the differences among flights in take-off time, climb duration and number of sampling points. EM-PCA missing-value imputation and functional principal component analysis compress the high-dimensional profiles containing missing values into low-dimensional score vectors, and a Transformer-based denoising diffusion model that treats the principal component scores as tokens is built in the score space. Energy-balance and thrust-feasibility constraints in the altitude domain are further derived from the BADA total energy model, converted into physical residuals that are differentiable with respect to the scores, and embedded into the training loss as SNR-weighted thresholded penalty terms, thereby reducing generated trajectories with energy mismatch or thrust exceedance. Experimental results show that PG-ClimbDiff achieves the best values of all four metrics, W1, MMD2, ED and ROCKET-FID, with W1, ED and ROCKET-FID reduced on average by 19.4%, 31.7% and 36.0% relative to the best baseline for each aircraft type; the time-domain trajectories obtained by integrating the profiles are smooth and plausible, free of anomalies such as near-level flat segments; and ablation experiments verify the effectiveness of the physical constraints and the Transformer denoising network, with the generated trajectories closely matching the real data in both altitude-domain statistics and time-domain morphology.

detail.abstract: Household surveys diagnose chronic disease from a single measurement of each respondent, treating each reading as a measure of a chronic state. We test whether they also measure the weather using 34,879 adults with a blood-pressure reading and 33,179 with a fasting glucose result from three rounds of the Bangladesh Demographic and Health Survey, merged with ERA5 temperature at the date and hour of measurement. Identification comes from day-to-day weather within a district and survey round, net of the district's seasonal pattern. A one-degree-Celsius rise in the daily maximum lowers systolic blood pressure on the day it is read by 0.562 mmHg, and a rise the day before an early-morning fasting test raises glucose by 1.028 mg/dL; haemoglobin, measured in one round, falls 0.018 g/dL per degree, and 0.037 against the wet bulb. The response is to humid heat: with both maxima entered together, the wet bulb keeps 1.208 mg/dL on glucose and −0.778 mmHg on pressure, while the dry-bulb term falls by two-thirds to three-quarters. The imprecise fall in haemoglobin points to dilution, arguing against dehydration as the source of the rise in glucose. The response moves the diagnosis: measured diabetes rises 0.626 and measured hypertension falls 0.839 percentage points per degree, while reported past diagnoses do not respond. Warmer 2022 fieldwork accounts for about a third of the 7.80-point rise in measured diabetes among adults aged 35 and over since 2017–18, a thermal component of the same order as the changes surveys are used to detect.

detail.abstract: This paper proposes a firm-level mechanism that explains why exchange-rate regimes are largely neutral with respect to real macro variables: exporters actively adjust marginal costs and markups to absorb nominal exchange-rate fluctuations. We quantify this mechanism using micro-level data from the European car market (1970–99). We show that floating regimes are associated with limited adjustment in destination-currency prices and limited response in quantities sold. We then estimate a structural demand-and-supply system to recover product-level markups and marginal costs. At breaks from pegged to floating regimes, producer-currency markups fall on impact by around 11% and marginal costs by 10%. A two-country real business cycle model with segmented financial markets, incorporating pricing-to-market and operational hedging, rationalises these patterns. Our model underscores the role of real micro rigidities, rather than nominal rigidities, in the weak transmission of exchange-rate fluctuations to real macro variables.

detail.abstract: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand is considering the case for a digital dollar, to complement tangible cash and make a more contemporary form of central bank money available to the general public. In addition to various economic, technological and policy choices, the creation of digital cash poses several legal challenges. This is because the existing legislation around central bank money – at least in its retail form – has historically regulated only the ability of central banks to issue bank notes in paper form and metallic coins. This article discusses to what extent digital cash can be stretched or squeezed into the conceptual taxonomies of traditional monetary law. Notably, it considers whether the current New Zealand legal framework is flexible enough to accommodate a default model for digital cash without law reform. In doing so, it reviews the legal basis for issuing digital cash under the existing legislation, discusses the initial agreed high-level features and focuses on some critical issues, inevitably subject to the (uncertain) final design choices.

detail.abstract: Tax scholars have made a number of breakthrough discoveries in tax law going back to at least Thomas Hobbes and his observations on a consumption tax almost 400 years ago. In more recent times, in the 1970 and 1980s, a number of tax law scholars made very important contributions in understanding the similarities and differences between an income tax, a consumption tax and a wage tax, as well as developing a greater understanding in a related area-the time value of money. It seems, however, that in the last 30 years or so, the only breakthrough or significant discovery in tax law is in the area of taxing "super-normal returns," sometimes referred to as "excess profits," "excess returns," or the economic term of "rents," and applying this greater knowledge to various areas of tax law. This has resulted, in some cases, questioning what has been generally accepted tax theories and policies.

detail.abstract: I develop a novel measure of carbon sensitivity in lending to assess reductions in portfolio exposure to brown assets. Using syndicated loan data, I show that countries with greater resistance to brown lending, proxied by economic development, experience faster shifts in the sectoral composition of loan portfolios. The decarbonization is driven primarily by domestic credit reallocation. I find consistent evidence of risk transfers to less regulated lenders and foreign countries, indicating arbitrage and incomplete regulations. Furthermore, lenders' climate risktaking and transfer behaviors vary sharply by syndicate role, loan type, and specialization. The existence of international trade in brown loans has important implications for supervisory evaluation. Using the European Central Bank's climate guide, I show that accounting for regulatory leakage reveals effects contrary to common wisdom.

detail.abstract: How does accountability operate when citizens cannot remove officials through elections? I develop a theory of strategic accountability in authoritarian hierarchies, in which rulers use hierarchical structures to impose governance accountability on subnational agents while retaining discretion over who bears responsibility and how far sanctions extend. The theory predicts that such accountability is substantive rather than purely rhetorical, rises with social damage, concentrates among lower-level officials, and produces inconsistent career impacts. I test these hypotheses using a combination of an original dataset on accountability following technological disasters in China from 2005 to 2024, a harmonized cross-national benchmark, and a unique official-level dataset on the career trajectories of Chinese county-level officials. Taken together, the findings identify a substantive but politically controlled form of accountability distinct from elections, responsiveness, and informal social discipline.

detail.abstract: Stocks with high idiosyncratic volatility (IVOL) earn low future returns, but not in every market state. I show that two simple investor beliefs can generate this pattern without short-sale constraints, trading costs, or stock-level controls: high risk deserves high reward, and a stock far from its benchmark is an opportunity. Investors therefore buy volatile stocks that have moved far from the benchmark, whether up or down, which pushes their prices too high, and the overpricing later reverses. The puzzle weakens when stocks move together, because deviations then carry little information, and deepens when stocks scatter. In this setting, the puzzle arises only from demand that does not depend on whether the stock rose or fell.

detail.abstract: This chapter examines the roles played by emerging countries in the international intellectual property regime. It begins by documenting the evolution of this regime—in particular, the rise of emerging countries and the regime’s changing geopolitical landscape. The chapter then explores the ramifications of such emergence, covering the middle path charted by these countries, their inconsistent positions at the global level, and the changing coalition dynamics within the World Trade Organization, the World Intellectual Property Organization and other international intergovernmental fora. This chapter concludes by identifying four primary roles emerging countries have played, and can play, in collaboration with other developing countries to strengthen the position of the developing world.

detail.abstract: We analyze how monetary policy uncertainty (MPU) affects bank credit allocation. First, we develop a theoretical model in which MPU consumes banks' risk-bearing capacity. Higher MPU therefore curbs risky lending, most strongly at less capitalized banks. Second, we test this prediction across U.S. credit markets using FOMC-announcement changes in optionimplied rate uncertainty, controlling for the monetary policy stance. In syndicated lending, a one standard deviation increase in MPU widens the gap between high-and low-capital banks in lending to riskier relative to safer borrowers by 1.65 percent. Small business and mortgage originations show similar patterns, consistent with this mechanism.

detail.abstract: Incomplete participation in social benefit programs is a persistent policy problem. We examine the role of paid preparers and software in tax credit take-up, shifting the focus from eligible recipients to the intermediaries who assist them. We partner with the Washington State Department of Revenue to conduct a field experiment examining whether informational interventions sent to paid preparers increase take-up of a low-income state tax credit. Preparers who are sent an informational letter file 0.30 to 1.09 more applications than preparers in a no-letter control group (a 9-33% increase). Results from different information treatments and additional analyses suggest that the letters worked by reducing determination costs and increasing the salience of the credit’s details. We then exploit a quasi-experiment in which a major self-preparation software provider integrated the application into its platform after previously only informing users of the credit. We estimate that claims among the provider’s users increased by approximately 233%, implying that 70% of the provider’s users who claimed the credit did so only because of the integration. Collectively, our results provide novel evidence that targeted outreach to tax preparers can be an effective policy tool, and that administrative frictions in social benefit take-up may be significantly larger than previously estimated.

detail.abstract: Does biodiversity regulatory exposure shape firms’ financing decisions? We examine this question by exploiting staggered Critical Habitat designations under the U.S. Endangered Species Act as unexpected shocks to firms’ biodiversity regulatory exposure. Recent designations increase the probability of a green vis-à-vis conventional bond issue, with the strongest response among firms in the least nature-dependent sectors and those without prior exposure. This surprise-salience pattern suggests that the financing response is stronger when biodiversity exposure is less anticipated. For exposed issuers, we find a significant greenium, which is attributable to a higher cost of conventional debt rather than cheaper green debt. Exposed green bond issuers are also more likely to make biodiversity commitments after issuance, but these commitments are short-lived and are not accompanied by quantified targets or measurable impact reductions. Consistent with this pattern, using hand-collected green bond documentation, we find that a larger share of exposed issuers revise their frameworks to include biodiversity, but this is not followed by greater allocation of proceeds to biodiversity projects. Overall, our findings suggest that firms’ preference for green debt reflects both relative financing costs and a visible expression of environmental commitment.

detail.abstract: Although the World Bank overhauled its procurement framework a decade ago, its bidder complaints process – an integral part of that framework – has not been updated to meet international best practices. The current process for bidder complaints affords relatively little transparency and accountability, and has been criticized (including by the U.S. Government Accountability Office) for failing to provide disappointed bidders an effective means of challenging failures in a procurement process. Reforming the Bank’s complaints process could be done by aligning it with international best practices, using (among other things) the benchmarks suggested by the Methodology for Assessment of Procurement Sys-tems (MAPS), which was developed with the support of the World Bank and the Organisation for Economic Co-Operation and Development (OECD) and which is regularly relied upon by the Bank. The complaints processes established by two other multilateral development banks, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and the European Investment Bank (EIB), also offer important benchmarks for reform. By updating its bid complaints process to meet international best practices, the World Bank could better ensure robust competition in the procurements it funds, bring to light more procurement failures for correction, and reinforce international confidence in the Bank’s important work.

detail.abstract: The study investigates the behavior of price, return, dependence, stationarity, outliers and robust regression of nine international metal futures (Aluminium, Copper, Gold, Lead, Palladium, Platinum, Silver, Tin and Zinc) in the period 2021-2025. The analysis employs descriptive statistics, Pearson's correlation coefficients, Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF), DF-GLS, Phillips-Perron (PP) and Kwiatkowski-Phillips-Schmidt-Shin (KPSS) tests and various outlier detection methods. The results show that the metals have significantly different return behavior and volatility. Correlation analysis shows that most metal futures move in the same direction. The stationarity tests indicate that monthly returns should be employed in econometric modeling. However, the results of the outlier detection differ in the Tukey, the Mean / Standard Deviation, Autoregressive Moving Average (ARMA) and the Wavelet methods, which shows the importance of the use of proper diagnostic techniques to detect extreme market observations. In this study, we also use M-estimation, S-estimation, and MM-estimation, which are robust regression methods, and Huber Type-I, Type-II, and Type-III standard errors and covariance specifications to check the relationships between the returns of Gold and the returns of the other metals. For the main robust regression specifications, the results are positive associations for Gold returns with Copper and Silver returns and a negative association for gold returns with Lead returns. Given the strength of the statistical significance to alternative covariance specifications we recommend MM-estimation with Huber Type-I covariance estimates as the preferred specification with Andrews M-estimation providing a useful robustness check. Finally, the results add to the knowledge of risk features and linkages of international metal futures markets, and have implications for portfolio diversification and commodity risk management.

detail.abstract: Russia and Germany both introduced compensation for unreasonable length of proceedings in response to pilot judgments of the European Court of Human Rights: Russia in 2010 after Burdov (No. 2), Germany in 2011 after Rumpf. Since Russia ceased to be a party to the Convention in 2022, its remedy has operated without the external benchmark it was built around. The statutory instruction to take the Strasbourg Court's practice into account in fixing the amount has disappeared, and the Supreme Court's guiding resolution now grounds the right in the Constitution and the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights. On 14 October 2026 the Presidium of the Russian Supreme Court approved Thematic Review No. 15/2026, which sets out fourteen legal positions on such claims. This paper analyses the Review against the German model of Sections 198 and 199 of the Courts Constitution Act. It compares the two remedies along five axes: scope, conditions of access, assessment of reasonableness, fault and harm, and the measure of compensation. The Review consistently widens access. It lets victims claim after four years even without a formal decision suspending the investigation, accepts challenges to procedural decisions as acceleration requests, refuses to let a court president's handling of such a request defeat the claim, and rejects budgetary shortfalls as an excuse for non-payment of judgments. In scope Russian law is now broader than German law. But none of the fourteen positions addresses the amount of compensation, which is where the German model is most determinate: a presumption of non-pecuniary harm and a flat rate of EUR 1,200 per year of delay, from which the court may depart. The paper argues that the loss of the Strasbourg benchmark makes a domestic scale the most urgent reform, and proposes an indicative annual amount, an explicit presumption of harm, and nonmonetary redress in criminal cases.

detail.abstract: Where term lending waits on a counterparty, the pricing of time is coupled to the pricing of credit risk, and in foul weather seizes up with it. Only a market filling every order at a risk-free rate could separate the two, but where no order is refused, trade cannot set the rate, and the clearing rate is made unobservable. In the prediction market specified here, forecasters' wagers set a curve of rates across term, and the loans and term deposits it writes are its book. Against the discrepancy between them, which the wagers move, forecasts are scored and forecasters paid in real time, zero-sum. In the literatures on prediction markets, with their scoring rules and wagering mechanisms, and on markets that direct what they forecast, no mechanism pays this way. Paying forecasters against what they move voids the guarantee of a proper scoring rule. Under a regularity condition on the economy, though, a curve keeps the book balanced at every term only if its rates are the clearing rates. Whatever anyone does, no wager loses more than its escrow, every winner is paid in full, and splitting or pooling wagers is worth nothing. Three attacks are priced but not closed. The mechanism relies on a credit tier to price credit and on a bank to post the overnight rate and carry the curve's net printing. No magnitude is determined in this paper, and whether forecasters bring the curve to the clearing rates, and how fast, is an open question.

detail.abstract: We investigate the impact of corporate environmental and social (ES) risks on the bank loan costs of peer firms linked through shared lenders. Using a regression discontinuity design centered on ES shareholder votes at U.S. public firms from 2005 to 2021, we find that the passage of these proposals results in an average 45-basis-point increase in the subsequent bank loan costs for peer firms. This effect is more pronounced for peers that are geographically closer to focal firms, less financially flexible, or have weaker ES performance, and when proposals resolve greater uncertainty. Surprisingly, the spillover is primarily driven by lenders with less expertise or weaker ex ante incentives to price ES risks. Our evidence suggests that, for these non-specialized banks, the passage of a focal proposal acts as an informational "wake-up call", prompting a reassessment of ES risks across their lending portfolios. These findings suggest that corporate ES risks affect not only individual firms but also their peers' borrowing costs through shared lenders.

detail.abstract: For centuries, gold has been widely accepted as a safe haven. However, since the rise of cryptocurrencies, Bitcoin has been a controversial investment option among market players worldwide. This research presents an empirical model that compares the two assets to determine which is the more attractive investment option. Based on a multidimensional framework, the study evaluates three major literature dimensions: historical profitability, risk & risk-adjusted performance, and asset decoupling. The methodology includes average monthly and annualized compound returns; skewness and kurtosis basic diagnostic; maximum drawdown; DPMO; average loss size (ALS); Sharpe and Sortino ratios; and Spearman correlations for hedge and safe-haven properties analysis. The sample period extends from July 2010 to May 2026, considering three structural time segments: a full period (2010-2026), a maturation stage (2014-2026), and a polycrisis stage (2020-2026). Additionally, several macroeconomic variables representing global economic flows were included, such as the NASDAQ, Dow Jones, S&P 500, oil prices, and major currency pairs. The empirical findings reveal that while Bitcoin initially compensated for its risk with exorbitant returns, in today's polycrisis economy, gold has proven to be a far more efficient asset, offering more than double the risk-adjusted return in comparison with Bitcoin. Furthermore, the results completely invalidate the argument that Bitcoin has stabilized as a safe haven fund, reinforcing its property as a speculative risk-on vehicle that intensifies its coupling with stock market benchmarks during periods of stress, among other findings. Ultimately, these insights aim to shed light how economic actors make decisions, depending on individual goals, the desired risk exposure, and their preferred portfolio diversification strategy.

detail.abstract: Background: Text-guided medical image segmentation combines visual appearance with descriptions of the target and its spatial context. However,geometric augmentation can invalidate directional phrases even when images and masks remain aligned. We introduce MedEquiSeg to couple image–mask augmentation with spatially consistent prompt updates.Methods: A compositional lexical map updates image-frame directions after flips and right-angle rotations. Frozen pooled BioMedCLIP embeddings condition a fine-tuned CLIP-RN50 network with complementary feature streams and two ATConv-equipped projectors. Five public benchmarks with target-derived referring captions were evaluated using three seeds and native-resolution scoring. A retrospective ordered configuration analysis, a separately matched BUSI phrase-remapping experiment, and fixed-model prompt controls assessed accuracy and text dependence. A private breastultrasound cohort with image-predicted prompts was analysed separately.Results: Across five public benchmarks, the complete MedEquiSeg configuration achieved macro-average Dice of 87.87% and IoU of 80.97%. Compared with the horizontal-flip-only multimodal baseline, it improved Dice by 1.46 percentage points (95% CI: 0.95–1.99) and IoU by 1.74 percentage points (95% CI: 1.13–2.34). MedEquiSeg achieved the highest macro-average Dice and IoU among the reproduced methods, although performance varied across datasets.Conclusions: The complete MedEquiSeg configuration improved five benchmark segmentation performance while explicitly maintaining spatial phrase correspondence under discrete augmentation. The results support joint evaluation of accuracy and text dependence; generalization to independently supplied clinical descriptions remains to be established. Code and supporting materials are available at https://github.com/zjj30/MedEquiSeg.

detail.abstract: Background: Machine-learning electrocardiography–impedance cardiography (ECG–ICG) timing methods are usually judged against conventional rules, which may be weaker than simple heart-rate or central-tendency predictors. We tested whether rule-relative gains reflect added waveform information or simple timing structure.,Methods: HeartCycle included 17 participants and 622 echocardiography (Echo)-matched beats; ReBeatICG included 21 participants and 1,588 annotated intervals; Belgrade included 20 participants and 21,015 intervals. Validation held out whole participants; ReBeatICG and Belgrade used Random Forests (RFs). Comparators included rules, training-set central tendency, R–R predictors and matched timing-only models. Mean absolute error (MAE), feature ablation and within-person tracking were assessed.,Results: HeartCycle B timing did not improve over the selected rule. Rule-relative MAE reductions were 14.46 ms (X), 11.21 ms (left ventricular ejection time, LVET) and 0.0150 (systolic time ratio, STR). R–R-only Ridge had lower X MAE than the feature workflow (17.92 versus 22.75 ms), and LVET MAEs were similar for the feature model, training mean and R–R-only Ridge (20.15, 20.25 and 20.07 ms); added morphology/time-frequency benefit was inconclusive. STR was not better than simple baselines after adjustment. Full versus combined-timing RF MAEs were 16.10 versus 15.59 ms in ReBeatICG and 6.82 versus 7.60 ms in Belgrade, where the small adjusted gain was of uncertain practical importance. Within-person correlations with Echo were weak (centred r 0.07–0.16).,Conclusion: Gains over conventional rules largely reflected heart-rate and timing structure rather than added waveform information, and lower error did not imply within-person tracking. Simple timing controls and within-person analyses should be reported before benefit is attributed to waveform features.

detail.abstract: Current automated systems for microbial identification from microscopic images remain constrained by poor transferability, sensitivity to staining quality, and a shortage of practical clinical explanations in everyday laboratory settings where time and expertise vary. Antimicrobial resistance heightens the need for rapid species-level identification beyond conventional culture-based methods. This paper reports MICRONet, a three-stage deep learning pipeline that jointly addresses all three limitations. Stage 1 uses a MobileNetV2-based binary gate to reject non-microscopic inputs, achieving 96.8% test accuracy and an area under the curve of 0.9945, with only 157 false positives and 167 false negatives on a 10,000-image test dataset. Stage 2 uses a two-phase fine-tuned EfficientNetB0 to classify images into ten microorganism categories (bacteria, fungi, and eight blood-cell types) at 92% test accuracy, with per-class area under the curve at or above 0.983. Stage 3 details our proposed Morphology-Aware Dual-Branch ConvNeXt V2 (MD-ConvNeXt V2), combining ArcFace angular-margin loss with our Quality-Guided Focal Loss (QGFL) for fine-grained species identification across 32 bacterial and 8 fungal classes, reaching 95.2% and 94.1% top-1 accuracy, respectively. A lightweight quality detector pre-trained on synthetic degradations provides a routing gate, reducing false positives on degraded inputs by 12.3 %.Explanations are generated using Smooth Grad-CAM++ and Contrastive Grad-CAM, which overlays positive and negative spatial activations on a single image. Ablation studies confirm that each component improves overall performance. The pipeline generates a species-level clinical report in under 60 s through a web-based interface, supporting low-resource clinical settings aligned with United Nations Sustainable Development Goals 3 and 9.

detail.abstract: Background and Objective: Image analysis for handheld trichoscopy is often developed on synthetic or public images before the device exists. We asked which components transfer from synthetic to real contact images, whether public dermoscopy supports absolute measurement, and which indicators remain stable when the capture changes.Methods: A measurement engine that computes scalp-condition grades from physical measurements was developed on a physically scaled procedural generator and tested on public-domain ISIC dermoscopy and 504 hand-labelled scalp tiles from two labelling rounds. Segmentation was compared by intersection over union (IoU), optical scale was measured from printed scale bars, and repeatability by the coefficient of variation under simulated re-capture. Confidence intervals (CIs) came from bootstrap resampling of source images and Wilson intervals; groups were compared with Mann–Whitney and Wilcoxon tests, and measurement methods by Bland–Altman analysis.Results: Synthetic-trained segmentation inverted its classes on real images. A trained segmenter and a classical black-hat extractor swapped rank with the labelling protocol: on labels corrected from classical seeds the extractor led by 0.103 IoU (95% CI 0.025–0.246); on labels drawn from blank masks by an independent annotator the network led by 0.116 (0.077–0.164). Site matching made no false matches (0/832) but recalled 25% of revisits. In 30 images with a printed scale bar, true sampling was 5.3–7.9 µm per pixel, and scale inferred from an assumed hair diameter erred by a median of +37% (29–59%). Under simulated re-capture, hair coverage and redness varied by 3.0–3.8% but shaft counts by 24.3%. Missed hair had lower contrast than detected hair but similar width.Conclusions: Synthetic data verified measurement code but did not train appearance models, and seeded evaluation labels appeared to favour the seeding algorithm. Density should be derived from follicles, and optical scale must be calibrated on the target device.

detail.abstract: Medical image segmentation requires multi-scale context without losing weakboundaries or transmitting excessive skip-feature clutter. We present EGD-MKANet, aconvolutional U-shaped network combining a Multi-Kernel Aggregation (MKA)bottleneck, Per-Channel Gated fusion (PCGate), multi-scale segmentation supervision,and auxiliary edge and distance-proxy tasks. MKA compresses channels before fourdepthwise dilated branches with rates {1, 2, 3, 5}, followed by grouped pointwise fusionand channel recalibration. It has a finite receptive field and linear spatial scaling forfixed channel width rather than content-adaptive global self-attention. PCGate learnspixel and channel-specific weights from decoder and skip features; the structural headsregularize shared representations during training but do not enter the gate. Across fivepolyp datasets, DSB2018 nuclei, and ISIC2018 skin lesions, EGDMKANet obtainsmDice values of 0.9412 on Kvasir-SEG, 0.9337 on DSB2018, and 0.9278 on ISIC2018,with BF1 values of 0.925 on Kvasir-SEG and 0.915 on DSB2018. In the EGDMKANet polyp and DSB2018 evaluations, a global thresh old is selected only on heldout validation data and then fixed for test inference; test masks are used solely formetric computation. detail.abstract: A rebalanced portfolio earns a harvest on rebalancing, but it pays for not letting its winners run. Both terms are realized cross-sectional variance, only measured at different horizons. This paper introduces an accounting that separates a portfolio's weighting plan and rebalance schedule from its trading clock and shows that the rebalance premium is isolated by varying the clock rather than the plan. This separation unifies three distinct literatures-contrarian microstructure, online portfolio selection, and stochastic portfolio theory-within a single discrete ledger. Varying the clock for a fixed plan cancels every first-order exposure pathwise and the resulting clock portfolio isolates a pure exposure to realized cross-sectional variances priced by the variance-ratio term structure. Under equal weights at a weekly horizon, we recover Lo and MacKinlay's 1990 contrarian strategy and generalize it here across plans, frequencies, and universes. Varying the plan on a fixed clock instead reduces both Cover's universal portfolio and Fernholz's diversity-weighted portfolio, up to third order, to fixed convex combinations of the rebalanced and buy-and-hold clocks of their respective anchor plans. The result is a tradeable two-sleeve proxy that predicts the universal portfolio's learning residual and identifies Fernholz's excess growth rate with the discrete daily harvest of our accounting. Measured net of costs across twenty-four capitalization and sector partitions of the U.S. equity cross-section over 2005-2026, this daily-against-monthly clock portfolio earns positive residual alpha in every partition and under every factor model considered, aggregating to 591 bps/yr on approximately 84% gross exposure with crisis-convex returns.

detail.abstract: The mathematics of European option pricing features a well-established formal connection to parabolic partial differential equations, yet many novice traders and finance students encounter moneyness, time value, implied volatility, and the Greeks as disconnected algebraic topics. This conceptual paper develops "Diwakar's Plate," a multi-layered visual teaching framework consisting of fixed concentric strike rings, a movable spot-price boundary, and an overlaid diffusion-value field. Its main contribution is not a new pricing equation, but a cognitive architecture that explicitly distinguishes the exact Black-Scholes-to-heat-equation mathematical transformation from an intuitive circular-plate metaphor. Calls and puts receive distinct spatial moneyness rules, intrinsic and extrinsic values are cleanly separated, and option Greeks (Delta, Gamma, Theta, Vega, Rho) are interpreted via defined spatial cues. A numerical NIFTY-style example illustrates the framework across all primary sensitivities, and a reproducible randomized classroom assessment protocol is proposed.

detail.abstract:
Electrification studies in Sub-Saharan Africa rarely connect national urban hierarchy with building-level spatial patterns of modeled electricity consumption. This study examined urban hub hierarchy and hub-distance gradients in Ghana, Senegal, and Uganda. IEA–MIT Building-level Electricity Access and Demand estimates for 354,567 buildings were combined with building footprints, VIIRS nighttime light (NTL) data, and WorldPop population estimates. DBSCAN identified 242 building clusters, of which 239 contained valid NTL-weighted centroids.

All three countries showed rank–size relationships, with NTL hierarchies being steeper than the population-based hierarchies. In the national building-weighted models, the estimated hub-distance elasticities were +0.251 in Ghana, +0.045 in Senegal, and −0.049 in Uganda. The two analyses did not order the countries in the same way: Uganda had the steepest NTL hierarchy but a coefficient that was not statistically distinguishable from zero. In addition, the country ordering was robust to alternative model specifications, although the Ghanaian estimate was sensitive to how hubs were defined and weighted. Estimates within individual hubs were closer to zero, and the coefficients for individual hubs varied in direction within every country. Therefore, national estimates do not represent a common center-periphery relationship across urban hubs.

The results support a national-to-local framework: national-level analysis can identify broad spatial patterns, but local policy decisions on infrastructure and electrification investment require hub-level assessment.

detail.abstract: The six Western Balkan economies will soon need AI supervisory institutions that none of them can comfortably staff alone. This paper proposes a Western Balkans AI Sandbox and Supervisory Network (WB-ASN): one shared regulatory sandbox and a pooled body of technical expertise, serving six national authorities that keep their full legal powers. Across the region, legal alignment and institutional capacity lag well behind digital infrastructure. This paper turns from that diagnosis to institutional design. The timing is set by Brussels. The Digital Omnibus on AI, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, moved the deadline for national sandboxes in Member States to 2 August 2027 and gave the AI Office a legal basis for an EUlevel sandbox. Obligations for stand-alone high-risk systems now apply from 2 December 2027. The region has roughly a year to put a compatible structure in place before its exporters face those rules without a home regulator to test against. The paper compares four institutional options, sets out a hub-and-spoke design, proposes financing through the Reform and Growth Facility and IPA III, and gives a three-phase roadmap to 2030.

detail.abstract: Prediction-market prices are traded state prices that can discipline the valuation of other financial claims exposed to the same event. After discount normalization, their level provides a risk-adjusted event probability, while their evolution can be used-under explicit recovery conditions-to measure how information about the event arrives over time. We combine these external event-state inputs with options that span event resolution and options that expire beforehand. Brexit provides a conventional FX benchmark, while the 2024 U.S. election and DJT provide a richer modern application. Event-spanning DJT options reveal a large and stable election exposure. Held-out pre-election calls are better explained once independently measured learning is incorporated, whereas puts display a distinct discrepancy. The results show how prediction markets and options can jointly identify event exposure, assess pre-resolution learning, and reveal market-specific frictions or additional structure.

detail.abstract:
The primitive recursor, F(x, y, Z) → x and F(x, y, S(n)) → G(y, F(x, y, n)), expresses counted iteration through a base case and a recursive step. Its step argument occurs in both the output and the continuing call. Related constructions appear in proof-assistant recursors, folds, and loop-carried state. The Primitive Recursor Test (PRT) evaluates 30 language models across 4,160 isolated sessions: 3,120 core sessions across ten tests and 1,040 auxiliary sessions across eight tests. Scoring separates the termination verdict, mathematical validity of the proof, and an additional rule-derived requirement. This requirement asks whether the decreasing comparison follows from the displayed rules. Mathematically valid proofs can use chosen symbol rankings or polynomial coefficients. A dependency-pair proof obtains the counter comparison from the recursive rule and uses an imported soundness theorem to establish termination.

On the two-rule recursor, 155/240 responses (64.6%) fail to supply a mathematically valid proof. On an eight-rule system containing the recursor, 122/480 responses (25.4%) give a wrong termination verdict and 400/480 (83.3%) fail mathematical proof assessment. Across 960 sessions on three open-construction tasks, 791 responses give the correct termination verdict; 516 of these (65.2%) lack a complete, mathematically valid proof. These outcomes include absent and incomplete arguments as well as refuted constructions. Mathematically valid rule-derived proofs occur in 2/240 recursor sessions and 0/480 eight-rule sessions. Given a menu of five mathematically valid methods, 452/480 sessions (94.2%) correctly classify the recursive-call method as both mathematically valid and rule-derived. The construction and menu tasks measure separate abilities: producing an argument and assessing a supplied method.

Across repetitions within at least one open task, 29 of 30 models change proof method and 13 reverse their termination verdict. With the eight-rule system's original symbols, 42 parseable path orders yield 23 rankings; polynomial coefficient maps differ in 45/46 within-model pairs. Among 34 returned reasoning records naming the recursive-call method, 33 fail to retain it as their final rule-derived proof. Under the follow-up's strict reading, models classify both of their two mathematically valid rule-derived recursor proofs as outside the requirement. Across 240 recursor follow-ups, mutual information between self-report and scored rule-derived success is 2.07% of the success label's entropy. The project repository provides the Lean 4 proof files and TTT2/CeTA certificates supporting the answer keys, all test-session records, and the full reproducibility pipeline. A Python rulebook computes scores from reader transcriptions; transcription errors can affect the assessments. The analysis relates proof classification to the information retained in response records and to the comparisons available within specified proof representations.

detail.abstract: Malaria remains a major public health issue. Indeed, according to the official WHO report dated December 4, 2025, 282 million cases of malaria were reported in 80 countries worldwide, resulting in 610,000 deaths. The prediction of malaria cases remains limited by the opacity of machine learning models and by the stationarity assumptions of classical Case-Based Reasoning approaches. This study introduces LoDiC-CBR (Local-Aware Directional Correction Case-Based Reasoning), an enhanced formulation that corrects two structural limitations of a prior CBR framework: insensitivity to the direction of epidemiological trends and a global computation that obscures national dynamics. LoDiC-CBR replaces the original correction constant with a signed, locally estimated term, computed within each geographic cluster from the signed mean of interannual variations, applying upward corrections in nations with sustained growth and downward corrections in nations with sustained decline. The approach is evaluated on a dataset: aggregated incidence across 54 African countries (2007-2017). LoDiC-CBR outperforms the original formulation and seven models with RMSE = 0.053%, MAE = 0.030%, and R2 = 94.5%, with superiority statistically confirmed by the Wilcoxon test and cross-validation. LoDiC-CBR preserves the native explainability of CBR, grounding each prediction in traceable historical cases a critical requirement for public health decision-support systems in resource-limited African contexts.

detail.abstract: Two candidates choose intervals evaluated by a Hurwicz criterion with worst-loss weight α. Under affine voting, the unique equilibrium is the median singleton for α ≥ 1/2; otherwise a common interval covers (1-2α)/(1α) of voters for any admissible distribution (the interquartile range under symmetry at α = 1/3). Under Downsian voting, every nondegenerate interval admits profitable trimming; pure equilibrium exists exactly when α ≥ 1/2, even for continuous, strictly increasing convex distance losses. Smooth neutral responses with positive slope at indifference make the affine interval a strict local equilibrium; sufficiently steep logistic voting eliminates pure equilibria.
